agenda_items.discussion_summary: Police Chief Jose Lopez presented the January–September 2015 crime report, reporting a 29% surge in Priority 1 calls, an average Priority 1 response time of 6 minutes 6 seconds (missing the 5:48 target and the 57% under-5-minute benchmark), 37 operational vacancies due to recruits in training, patrol district staffing ranging from 42% to 72%, and his October White House discussion with President Obama on DPD diversion programs. During questioning, a council member cited a report showing Black residents accounted for over 80% of misdemeanor marijuana charges (and 46% among those under 25 despite being 15% of the population) even after council reforms; Lopez stated he had not read the report, denied marijuana arrests were a DPD priority, and suggested concerned individuals should not smoke marijuana.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing on HOPWA Funding Allocation and Administrative Barriers
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle-section omission in the transcript digest, Council concluded a public hearing on Housing Opportunities for Persons with AIDS (HOPWA) funding where a speaker urged Council to remove administrative funding barriers preventing specialized emergency shelter and affordable housing organizations from participating fully. Council questioned Community Development staff regarding the transition from state administration to City of Durham entitlement jurisdiction and whether upcoming one-year funds could support housing rather than solely services, noting policy barriers affecting agencies such as the Durham Crisis Response Center.

agenda_items.title: Economic Development Incentive Agreement: Frontier Communications of the Carolinas LLC
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Daryl Solomon of the Office of Economic and Workforce Development presented a job creation incentive agreement with Frontier Communications of the Carolinas LLC, noting that media coverage had prematurely reported the deal prior to Council action. Durham Chamber of Commerce Vice President of Economic Development Ted Conner spoke in support of the project during the public hearing, and Council approved the agreement 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Economic Development Incentive Agreement: WillowTree, Inc.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Daryl Solomon presented an incentive agreement not to exceed $70,500 with mobile strategy and software firm WillowTree, Inc. (represented by Tobias Dengel) projected to create 98 jobs by the end of 2018 at an average annual salary of $84,118 with full benefits and use of the NCWorks Career Center. Ted Conner of the Chamber of Commerce highlighted that roughly 40% of WillowTree's hires come from coding schools rather than computer science degrees, creating workforce opportunities with Durham Public Schools and Durham Tech, and Council approved the agreement after closing the vote without dissent.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (tally not announced aloud in transcript)

votes.item_title: Approve City Manager's Priority Items (Items 4, 10, 11, and Supplemental Item 14)
votes.discussion_detail: City Manager Tom Bonfield presented priority revisions correcting exhibit numbering on Item 4, inserting company names into Items 10 and 11, and adding the Q3 crime report and Civilian Police Review Board / Human Relations Commission updates as Item 14. Council approved the priority items 7-0.

votes.item_title: Economic Development Incentive Agreement: Frontier Communications of the Carolinas LLC (Item 10)
votes.notes: Revised from Project Ironman / Cavalier placeholder in Manager's priority items.
votes.discussion_detail: OEWD staff presented the job-creation incentive agreement with Frontier Communications of the Carolinas LLC, and Durham Chamber of Commerce VP Ted Conner testified in favor. Following closure of the public hearing without opposition, Council approved the agreement 7-0.

votes.item_title: Economic Development Incentive Agreement: WillowTree, Inc. (Item 11)
votes.notes: Transcript ends vote at 'Close vote. Thank you.' without an audible tally announcement; no dissent voiced.
votes.discussion_detail: OEWD staff presented an incentive payment not to exceed $70,500 for WillowTree, Inc. to create 98 mobile engineering and design jobs averaging $84,118 annually by end of 2018. Ted Conner spoke in support, the public hearing closed with no opposition, and Mayor Bell opened and closed the vote before Council Member Don Moffitt thanked staff for securing both job-creation deals.

meetings.title: Durham City Council November 2, 2015
meetings.executive_summary: With all seven members present, the Durham City Council presented three ceremonial proclamations, referred a HOPWA contract with Duke University back to Community Development while adding fiscal impact analyses to two historic landmark cases (7-0), and adopted the remaining consent agenda (7-0), including a 28-acre Lake Michie expansion acquisition and Water Management unconscious bias training. On the general business agenda, Council unanimously approved the Family Fare companion zoning map change at 4116 NC 55 Highway (7-0), TROSA's outdoor display rezoning on Roxboro Road (7-0), the Imperial Tobacco Building historic landmark designation at 215 Morris Street (7-0), and the Leesville/Andrews consolidated annexation (7-0). On Item 18, the Wiley and Elizabeth Forbes House local historic landmark designation at 3307 Devon Road (LD150002), Council passed the designation in a 5-2 split vote with Mayor Bill Bell, Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden, Steve Schewel, Eddie Davis, and Don Moffitt voting Aye and Eugene Brown and Diane Catotti voting Nay.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations and Housing Authority Oath of Office
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presented three proclamations recognizing the 50th anniversary of the Durham Soil and Water Conservation District, November 2015 as Celebration of Health Month / American Diabetes Month with the Durham Diabetes Coalition, and Long-Term Care Awareness with remarks by Dale Matial. The City Clerk also swore in Gloria M. Nottingham for reappointment to the Durham Housing Authority Board of Commissioners.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items and Consent Agenda Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield referred Item 4 (HOPWA contract with Duke University) back to Community Development and added fiscal impact analyses to historic landmark Items 18 and 19 (approved 7-0). Council then adopted the remaining consent agenda 7-0, covering the acquisition of 28 acres at 1902 Camden Avenue for Lake Michie facility expansion, unconscious bias training for Water Management, a fourth amendment with the Durham Bulls for the Durham Athletic Park, East Main Street culvert stabilization (SD-2015-01), an Alston Avenue widening (U-3308) CSX railroad encroachment agreement, and a Waste Industries transfer station memo.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment: Family Fare (A1400012)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff member Pat Young presented a Future Land Use Map amendment submitted by Horvath Associates, P.A. to change 1.34 acres at Fletcher Road and 4116 NC 55 Highway from Recreation/Open Space to Commercial for a proposed gas station and convenience store, noting a 9-3 Planning Commission recommendation of approval. Applicant Ron Horvath spoke briefly and the public hearing closed; the formal vote occurred inside an omitted middle segment of the transcript digest prior to the companion zoning hearing.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Omitted in transcript gap (proceeded to companion rezoning)

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Family Fare (4116 NC 55 Highway / Fletcher Road)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council considered the companion zoning map change for the Family Fare site above the floodplain elevation. Council Member Diane Catotti questioned staff regarding the rezoned boundary relative to the floodplain and a proffered trail right-of-way dedication along the western creek edge, which applicant Ron Horvath confirmed. Council passed both the rezoning and the statutory consistency statement 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: TROSA Roxboro Outdoor Display (Z1500004)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pat Young presented TROSA's rezoning request for a 13.74-acre Roxboro Road parcel. Representative Dan Jewell (Coulter Jewell Thames) explained that TROSA sought to rope off 70,000 square feet of parking lot for up to three week-long seasonal outdoor sales annually while retaining ordinance-compliant parking and removing display merchandise indoors each night under UDO outdoor display rules. Council passed both the rezoning and consistency statement 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Local Historic Landmark Designation: Wiley and Elizabeth Forbes House (LD150002)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pat Young presented a request to designate the Wiley and Elizabeth Forbes House at 3307 Devon Road—one of the first 20 structures built in Hope Valley—as a local historic landmark, accompanied by a newly added fiscal impact analysis reflecting property tax impacts. Following omitted middle discussion, Council passed the designation in a 5-2 split vote, with Eugene Brown and Diane Catotti voting no.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 5-2 (Ayes: Bell, Cole-McFadden, Schewel, Davis, Moffitt; Nays: Brown, Catotti)

agenda_items.title: Local Historic Landmark Designation: Imperial Tobacco Building (LD150003)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pat Young presented Measurement Incorporated's application to designate the Imperial Tobacco Building at 215 Morris Street as a local historic landmark for its contributions to Durham's tobacco history, accompanied by a fiscal impact analysis. With no public speakers, Council approved the designation 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation: Leesville/Andrews Residential (BDG1500002)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pat Young presented a consolidated annexation for a single-family residential development, reporting adequate water/sewer capacity, a revenue-positive fiscal impact analysis, and a 10-0 Planning Commission recommendation. In response to Council Member Diane Catotti, the applicant confirmed dedication of right-of-way along its frontage including a 5-foot sidewalk and 4-foot bike lane. Council passed both the annexation/zoning motion and the consistency statement 7-0.

votes.item_title: Approve City Manager's Priority Items (Refer Item 4 HOPWA Contract; Add Fiscal Impact Analyses to Items 18 & 19)
votes.discussion_detail: City Manager Tom Bonfield referred Item 4 (HOPWA contract with Duke University) back to Community Development and added fiscal impact analyses to the Wiley and Elizabeth Forbes House (Item 18) and Imperial Tobacco Building (Item 19) landmark designation packets. Council approved the priority items 7-0.

votes.item_title: Zoning Map Change: Family Fare (4116 NC 55 Highway / Fletcher Road)
votes.discussion_detail: Following questions from Council Member Diane Catotti on floodplain boundaries and western creek trail right-of-way dedication proffered by Ron Horvath, Council closed the public hearing and approved the Family Fare companion rezoning 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for Family Fare Rezoning
votes.discussion_detail: Council adopted the statutory consistency statement for the Family Fare zoning map change 7-0.

votes.item_title: Zoning Map Change: TROSA Roxboro Outdoor Display (Z1500004)
votes.discussion_detail: After Dan Jewell clarified that TROSA's 70,000-square-foot parking lot area would host up to three seasonal outdoor display sales per year with merchandise brought inside overnight and compliant remaining parking, Council approved the rezoning 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for TROSA Rezoning (Z1500004)
votes.discussion_detail: Council adopted the statutory consistency statement for TROSA's Roxboro Road rezoning 7-0.

votes.item_title: Local Historic Landmark Designation: Wiley and Elizabeth Forbes House (LD150002)
votes.notes: Clerk initially announced 6-1 with Brown voting no, then corrected to 5-2 with Brown and Catotti voting no.

After the clerk initially misread the tally as 6-1, she corrected the official result to 5-2 with Eugene Brown and Diane Catotti voting no.

votes.item_title: Local Historic Landmark Designation: Imperial Tobacco Building (LD150003)

meetings.title: Durham City Council October 19, 2015
meetings.executive_summary: With all seven members present, the Durham City Council presented proclamations for National Lead Poisoning Prevention Week and Conflict Resolution Day, added two supplemental economic development incentive agreements (Projects Cavalier and Ironman) as priority items (7-0), and approved the consent agenda excluding pulled Item 11 (7-0), including a resolution supporting Syrian refugee resettlement in Durham and a report on child sex trafficking. Council unanimously approved the Denfield Street annexation for True Covenant Baptist Church (7-0) after hearing an adjacent owner's runoff concerns, removed local historic landmark designation from West Village Complex Parcel L (LD1500001, 7-0) after weighing its 50% property tax deferral against redevelopment plans, approved preliminary incentive agreements for Project Cavalier (unanimous) and Project Ironman (7-0), and approved acquiring the former Duke Diet and Fitness Center property (7-0) as an urban wetland/stormwater site with potential future park amenities.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations (Lead Poisoning Prevention & Conflict Resolution) and Council Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presented a National Lead Poisoning Prevention Week proclamation to PEACH program director Lenore Smith, noting a Mayor's Poverty Reduction Initiative survey finding that about 70% of Northeast Central Durham residents in older housing needed interior repairs, and a Conflict Resolution Day proclamation to the Elna B. Spaulding Conflict Resolution Center for peer mediation in eight Durham schools and truancy court. Council Member Eddie Davis reported on volunteer brush clearing at Geer Cemetery ahead of the 150th anniversary of the 13th Amendment, and Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden thanked the City Manager for assisting students at Lakeview School.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items (26 & 27) and Consent Agenda Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield added supplemental Items 26 and 27 (preliminary economic development incentive agreements for Project Cavalier and Project Ironman), which Council approved 7-0. Council then adopted the consent agenda 7-0—pulling Item 11 (Duke Diet & Fitness Center acquisition) for discussion—covering FY 2015-16 budget carryovers, temporary special-event street closing rules, Jordan Lake Partnership support, Lake Michie advance land acquisition, Achievement Academy lease/services, a report on child sex trafficking, and a resolution supporting Syrian refugee resettlement in Durham.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation: Denfield Street / True Covenant Baptist Church
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following an omitted middle segment in the digest, Council heard public testimony on the Denfield Street annexation for True Covenant Baptist Church. Diane King spoke in favor of the church's plans, while adjoining landowner Samuel Mebane stated he did not oppose the church itself but raised concerns about 50 years of tires, motor parts, and contaminated runoff draining from 4512–4516 Denfield Street into a nearby creek. Council approved the annexation and its consistency statement 7-0.

agenda_items.title: West Village Complex Parcel L Local Historic Landmark Designation Removal (LD1500001)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff member Pat Young presented an application to remove local historic landmark status from West Village Complex Parcel L, noting a 6-0 recommendation from the Historic Preservation Commission and preliminary redevelopment discussions by the owner. Council Member Diane Catotti asked about the consequences of removing Certificate of Appropriateness oversight, and another council member pointed out that retaining landmark designation on redeveloped property would entitle the owner to a 50% property tax reduction compared to 100% taxation if removed. Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden moved approval, which passed 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Preliminary Economic Development Incentive Agreement: Project Cavalier
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Office of Economic and Workforce Development Director Kevin Dick presented a preliminary incentive agreement for Project Cavalier within the community redevelopment area. Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden moved approval and a council member praised the incentives as a bargain while urging future agreements to offer stronger incentives for hiring city residents. The item passed without opposition.

agenda_items.title: Preliminary Economic Development Incentive Agreement: Project Ironman
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed the preliminary economic development incentive agreement for Project Ironman. A council member requested separating custom-eligibility on-the-job training grant funds from the city incentive in the final agreement, to which staff agreed. Council approved the preliminary agreement 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Acquisition of Former Duke Diet and Fitness Center Property
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled from the consent agenda, Council reviewed the proposed acquisition of the former Duke Diet and Fitness Center property primarily for a high-profile urban wetland and stormwater project. Council discussion emphasized integrating park and recreation amenities and site design into the project scope early on and considering facility upgrades as a candidate for a future parks and recreation bond referendum before approving the acquisition 7-0.

votes.item_title: Approve City Manager's Priority Items (Add Supplemental Items 26 & 27)
votes.discussion_detail: City Manager Tom Bonfield requested adding supplemental Items 26 and 27 (preliminary economic development incentive agreements for Project Cavalier and Project Ironman) as priority items, and Council approved 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consent Agenda (Items 1-10, 12-15, 25; excluding pulled Item 11)
votes.notes: Item 11 pulled for public speakers and heard separately; Items 16-19 heard on General Business Agenda.
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Bell pulled Item 11 (Duke Diet & Fitness Center acquisition) for speakers, and Council adopted the remaining consent agenda 7-0, including Housing Appeals Board/Workforce Development Board/Housing Authority appointments, FY 2015-16 budget carryovers, special-event street closing revisions, Lake Michie advance acquisition, Achievement Academy lease/contract, child sex trafficking report, and Syrian refugee resettlement support resolution.

votes.item_title: Consolidated Annexation: Denfield Street Property (True Covenant Baptist Church)
votes.discussion_detail: Following testimony from Diane King in favor of True Covenant Baptist Church's Denfield Street annexation and adjacent owner Samuel Mebane regarding long-standing debris and creek runoff at 4512–4516 Denfield Street, Council closed the public hearing and approved the item 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for Denfield Street Property
votes.discussion_detail: Council adopted the statutory consistency statement for the Denfield Street annexation and zoning 7-0.

votes.item_title: Local Historic Landmark Designation Removal: West Village Complex Parcel L (LD1500001)
votes.discussion_detail: Pat Young presented the Historic Preservation Commission's 6-0 recommendation to remove local historic landmark status from West Village Parcel L. Council discussed Certificate of Appropriateness implications (Diane Catotti) and noted that keeping landmark status on a redeveloped lot would cut future property taxes by 50%. Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden moved approval, passing 7-0.

votes.notes: Mayor Pro Tem Cole-McFadden initially moved; another council member moved/seconded; clerk announced passage without numerical count in transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: OEWD Director Kevin Dick presented Project Cavalier within the community redevelopment area. A council member voiced support while encouraging higher incentives for employing city residents in future deals, and the clerk announced 'It passes' without stated dissent.

votes.discussion_detail: Following confirmation that staff would separate custom-eligibility on-the-job training grant funds in the agreement, Council approved the preliminary economic development incentive agreement for Project Ironman 7-0.

meetings.title: Durham City Council October 5, 2015
meetings.executive_summary: With all seven members present, the Durham City Council presented proclamations for Imagine a Day Without Water, National Arts and Humanities Month (featuring Piedmont Laureate James Maxey), and Long-Term Care Residents' Rights, and unanimously approved the consent agenda (7-0) including making the Mayor's Hispanic/Latino Committee an official committee and selling property interests for Parkside at Morris Street. Council opened Item 4 regarding a letter to GoTriangle endorsing the recommended preferred alternative for the Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit Draft EIS (modified per Council Member Eddie Davis's input) before an omitted middle portion of the transcript digest. Council subsequently unanimously approved the Hanover Point Subdivision rezoning (7-0) removing an unbuildable East Horseshoe Road widening commitment, adopted UDO Text Amendment TC1500005 on accessory structures and home occupations (7-0), and approved a $6 million, 15-year economic development incentive agreement with Wexford Chesterfield Parking LLC (7-0) to redevelop 701 West Main Street into downtown life-science lab and Class A office space.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations and Southside Parade of Homes Recognition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presented proclamations for Imagine a Day Without Water (Oct. 6) to Water Management Assistant Director Vicki Westbrook, National Arts and Humanities Month to Durham Arts Council Executive Director Sherry DeVries and Piedmont Laureate James Maxey, and Long-Term Care Residents' Rights to local care home committees. Council also congratulated those involved in Southside revitalization on featuring a new South Street home in the regional Parade of Homes.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no priority items from the City Attorney or City Clerk, Council unanimously approved the consent agenda covering minutes, street and infrastructure acceptances, generator maintenance, the August 2015 bid report, an easement with Impress Development LLC at 112 West Main Street, an upset-bid sale at 110 Chestnut Street, property sales to Lambert Development Hunt Street LLC for Parkside at Morris Street, DOT Sign and Signal Shop design services, and granting official committee status to the Mayor's Hispanic/Latino Committee.

agenda_items.title: Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit Project Draft EIS Endorsement Letter
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation staff member Wesley Carroll presented a revised letter to GoTriangle endorsing the recommended preferred alternative in the Durham-Orange Light Rail Draft Environmental Impact Statement, incorporating edits requested by Council Member Eddie Davis following its September 21 deferral and public hearings held September 29 and October 1. Mayor Bell noted council members had additional proposed edits and called public speakers Mark Iwinski and Dan Jewell, while discussion touched on engineering and cost constraints against relocating the Alston Avenue transit station east of Alston Avenue; the vote occurred in an omitted segment of the digest.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Hanover Point Subdivision
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Attorney Patrick Byker (Morningstar Law Group), representing Lennar Carolinas, requested rezoning to remove a 2006 commitment requiring 33-foot curb-and-gutter improvements on East Horseshoe Road because Public Works determined existing structures, drainage, and topography prevented meeting stormwater standards. NCDOT approved alternative neighborhood access improvements already under construction, Planning Commission unanimously recommended approval, and Council approved the rezoning (7-0) and consistency statement.

agenda_items.title: UDO Text Amendment: Accessory Structures and Home Occupations (TC1500005)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff member Michael Stock presented a text amendment to UDO Section 5.4 requested by Parker Poe on behalf of Travis Feltz to allow accessory structures beside a primary structure in RS-20 lots of at least two acres in suburban/rural tiers and to explicitly permit accessory structures for all home occupations. The amendment had been recommended 14-0 by the Planning Commission and approved 5-0 by the Board of County Commissioners. Council passed the text amendment (7-0) and its consistency statement.

agenda_items.title: Economic Development Incentive Agreement: Wexford Chesterfield Parking LLC (701 W. Main Street)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: OEWD Director Kevin Dick, joined by Dan Kramer and Justin Parker of Wexford Science and Technology, presented an incentive agreement providing $6 million over 15 years to adaptively reuse the historic Chesterfield Building at 701 West Main Street into life-science laboratory and Class A office space (amid a 6% downtown office vacancy rate) with structured parking, a 40-year public-use reservation, and funded youth internships. Council members praised the private investment, job creation, and positive property tax cash flow while requesting efforts to preserve George Roesch's blue-circle stairwell painting, and approved the agreement 7-0.

votes.item_title: Zoning Map Change: Hanover Point Subdivision
votes.discussion_detail: Patrick Byker on behalf of Lennar Carolinas presented the rezoning to remove an unbuildable 2006 commitment for East Horseshoe Road curb-and-gutter widening, noting NCDOT-approved alternate access under construction and unanimous Planning Commission support. No public opposition appeared, and Council approved the rezoning 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for Hanover Point Subdivision Rezoning
votes.notes: Clerk closed the vote without speaking the numerical tally aloud.
votes.discussion_detail: Council voted to adopt the statutory consistency statement for the Hanover Point rezoning immediately after the 7-0 rezoning vote, closing the vote without dissent before moving to the final planning item.

votes.item_title: UDO Text Amendment: Accessory Structures and Home Occupations (TC1500005)
votes.discussion_detail: Michael Stock presented UDO Section 5.4 amendments regarding RS-20 side-yard accessory structures on 2+ acre suburban/rural lots and allowing accessory structures for all home occupations, noting 14-0 Planning Commission and 5-0 BOCC approval. Council passed the amendment 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for UDO Text Amendment (TC1500005)
votes.notes: Clerk closed the vote without speaking the numerical tally aloud.
votes.discussion_detail: Council voted on the statutory consistency statement for TC1500005 immediately after the 7-0 ordinance vote; the clerk closed the vote without dissent.

votes.item_title: Economic Development Incentive Agreement: Wexford Chesterfield Parking LLC (Item 19)
votes.discussion_detail: OEWD Director Kevin Dick presented the $6 million, 15-year city incentive for Wexford's adaptive reuse of the 701 West Main Street Chesterfield Building into life-science labs, Class A office space, and structured parking, alongside county incentives, tax credits, youth internships, and a 40-year public-use parking agreement. Council praised the positive cash flow and tax base growth and approved the agreement 7-0.

meetings.title: Durham City Council September 21, 2015
meetings.executive_summary: With all seven members present, the Durham City Council proclaimed October 2015 as National Disability Employment Awareness Month, heard an update on Southside homeownership underwriting hurdles, and unanimously approved the consent agenda (7-0) including a Disparity Study follow-up, an open data platform contract, and Alston Avenue widening property conveyances. On the general business agenda, Council unanimously approved the 729 Lawson Drive consolidated annexation (7-0), an unidentified planning/SPU item and its consistency statement (7-0), and the Beaman Street closing for Southside Phase 2 (7-0). On an economic development incentive agreement for the Morris Street Phase 1 office/lab and structured parking project (C1, C2, P1), Council passed the deal in a 6-1 split vote—with Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Eugene Brown, Steve Schewel, Eddie Davis, and Don Moffitt voting Aye and Diane Catotti voting Nay over the size of the incentive percentage—before hearing closing remarks on policing from Steve Schewel and Durham Police Officers Association President Mike Evans.

agenda_items.title: National Disability Employment Awareness Month, Southside Update, and CAC Oath
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presented the October 2015 National Disability Employment Awareness Month proclamation to Jason Jones, Mars Clemens, and Deborah Giles. A brief staff snippet noted strong family interest in Phase 1 Southside homeownership alongside underwriting barriers at initial mortgage application, and a Citizens Advisory Committee appointee took the oath of office.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously adopted the consent agenda covering minutes, the June 2015 inventory audit, Ridgeway Road street renamings (SN1500002/SN1500003), a North Parking Garage lease amendment with American Campus LLC, stream relocation maintenance contracts, Water Management roof replacements, the Disparity Study follow-up report, insurance broker and harm-reduction service contracts, NCDOT property conveyances for the Alston Avenue widening project, and an open data platform contract.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation: 729 Lawson Drive (BDG1500003)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff member Pat Young presented a consolidated annexation, initial zoning, and utility extension agreement for 729 Lawson Road in the Jordan Lake B watershed, noting unanimous April 14 Planning Commission support, adequate utility capacity, and positive fiscal impact. The applicant explained he sought annexation to connect to an existing city water line (with county sewer already available), and staff confirmed adjacent properties were expected to annex by year-end to establish contiguity. Council approved the annexation (7-0) and its consistency statement.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation: Harris Beverage, 1035 Junction Road (BDG1500009)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pat Young presented a consolidated annexation for 21.5 acres at 1035 Junction Road with adequate utility capacity and positive fiscal impact, explaining in response to Council Member Steve Schewel that a standing 10-year Planning Commission policy automatically endorses current zoning translations. Attorney Patrick Byker spoke for Harris Beverage; the vote occurred in an omitted middle segment of the digest.

agenda_items.title: Planning/Zoning Item Involving Special Use / SPU Concerns
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a digest gap, Council concluded discussion referencing continuing staff concerns regarding a special use / SPU matter and voted 7-0 to approve the item and 7-0 to adopt its consistency statement.

agenda_items.title: Street Closing: Beaman Street (SC1500004)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pat Young presented a request by Mike Tarrant of Stewart Engineering to close all 422 linear feet of Beaman Street, bordered by a place of worship and vacant land for Southside Phase 2 residential redevelopment, dividing the right-of-way evenly among adjoining owners with no negative agency impacts. Tarrant appeared for questions and asked for support for Southside Phase 2, and Council approved the street closing 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Economic Development Incentive Agreement: Morris Street Phase 1 Development (C1, C2, P1)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic development staff presented a multi-phase downtown development along Morris Street terminating at Duke Street near the Carmichael Building, focusing Phase 1 on office/lab buildings C1 and C2, structured parking P1, and the Morris Green open space amid a 6% downtown Class A office vacancy rate, with a roughly seven-year overall buildout. During debate following Vince Taylor's public remarks, a supporting council member agreed with Diane Catotti that the city's incentive percentage was high and urged pushing future deals toward 50-50 parity, while still voting yes; Council passed the agreement 6-1 with Catotti voting no.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 6-1 (Ayes: Bell, Cole-McFadden, Brown, Schewel, Davis, Moffitt; Nay: Catotti)

agenda_items.title: Police Staffing Remarks and Public Comment Supporting Chief Jose Lopez
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Steve Schewel addressed active and former police officers in the gallery to thank them and invite them to discuss their concerns over pizza after the meeting, prompting Mayor Bell to interject that he was presiding over the meeting. Durham Police Officers Association President Mike Evans then addressed Council on behalf of roughly 500 members in support of Police Chief Jose Lopez, disputing claims of low morale and rising crime and urging greater unity between city leadership and the department.

votes.item_title: Consolidated Annexation: 729 Lawson Drive (BDG1500003)
votes.discussion_detail: Pat Young presented the consolidated annexation for 729 Lawson Road (city water, county sewer) with unanimous Planning Commission support and positive fiscal impact, and the applicant requested approval to tap into the existing city water main. Council approved the annexation 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for 729 Lawson Drive (BDG1500003)
votes.notes: Clerk closed the vote without speaking the numerical tally aloud.
votes.discussion_detail: Council voted on the statutory consistency statement for 729 Lawson Drive immediately after the 7-0 annexation vote; the clerk closed the vote without dissent.

votes.notes: Item title and number omitted in transcript digest gap between 00:28:11 and 00:51:21.
votes.discussion_detail: Following a middle truncation in the transcript digest after Item 21, Council concluded remarks acknowledging staff concerns about an SPU matter and approved the item 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for Unidentified Planning/Zoning Item
votes.discussion_detail: Council adopted the statutory consistency statement for the preceding planning item 7-0.

votes.item_title: Street Closing: Beaman Street (SC1500004)
votes.discussion_detail: Pat Young presented Stewart Engineering's request to close 422 linear feet of Beaman Street adjacent to a place of worship and Southside Phase 2 redevelopment land, with no adverse agency impacts. Council approved the street closing 7-0.

votes.item_title: Economic Development Incentive Agreement: Morris Street Phase 1 Development (C1, C2, P1)
votes.notes: Wait-listed/disputed over incentive size; Diane Catotti cast the sole dissenting vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Staff presented Phase 1 of the Morris Street development (C1 and C2 office/lab buildings, P1 parking, and Morris Green open space) to address Durham's 6% downtown Class A office vacancy. A council member noted it was a close call and echoed Diane Catotti's concern about reducing future downtown incentive percentages toward a 50-50 level relative to county incentives, while voting in favor; Council passed the agreement 6-1 with Catotti voting no.

disagreements.issue: Size of Economic Development Incentive for Morris Street Phase 1 Development (C1, C2, P1)
disagreements.summary: Council divided 6-1 over an economic development incentive agreement for Phase 1 of the Morris Street office, laboratory, and structured parking project near the Carmichael Building. While six members voted yes to deliver needed Class A downtown office space and structured parking, Council Member Diane Catotti voted no over the high incentive percentage.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the Phase 1 Morris Street economic development incentive agreement
side_a_arguments: Downtown Class A office vacancy is only 6%, causing Durham to lose prospective employers without new office and lab space.
Structured parking is required to capitalize the multi-phase development and achieve a competitive market return.
While acknowledging the incentive percentage is high, supporters opted to approve this deal while pushing to lower future incentive percentages toward a 50-50 split as downtown strengthens.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose the incentive agreement due to excessive city incentive percentage
side_b_arguments: Objected to the large city incentive percentage relative to the project and growing strength of the downtown market (referenced by supporting colleague at 01:25:45).
disagreements.resolution: Passed 6-1

meetings.title: Durham City Council September 8, 2015
meetings.executive_summary: With all seven members present, the Durham City Council inducted the 2015–2016 Durham Youth Commission, issued proclamations for Constitution Week, Life Insurance Awareness Month, and National Recovery Month, and heard Mayor Bill Bell's reminder that public comments on the Durham-Orange Light Rail Draft EIS must go directly to GoTriangle by October 13. Following an omitted middle portion of the transcript digest, Council debated architectural alternatives for the new police headquarters—specifically weighing whether spending $4 million to preserve the historic Carpenter Chevrolet building was justified—and reached consensus to defer the design for additional apples-to-apples review at an upcoming work session. On Item 15, the US 70 Self Storage Center rezoning (Z1400020) that the Planning Commission had recommended denying 1-10, Council passed the rezoning in a 5-2 split vote (Ayes: Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Eugene Brown, Steve Schewel, and Don Moffitt; Nays: Diane Catotti and Eddie Davis) after the applicant proffered a permanent access easement covenant, before unanimously adopting the consistency statement (7-0) and concluding with a Council Member Eddie Davis-led reflection on community violence.

agenda_items.title: Durham Youth Commission Induction, Proclamations, and Council Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council inducted the 2015–2016 Durham Youth Commission after hearing a report on 2014–2015 committee projects (including Black Wall Street web episodes, Week of No Barriers, and safe-dating workshops), and presented proclamations for Constitution Week, Life Insurance Awareness Month, and National Recovery Month. Council Member Eddie Davis announced December 5–6 Geer Cemetery events honoring the 150th anniversary of the 13th Amendment and noted the death of former Council Member George Nixon, Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden praised DYC and asked staff to investigate an employee benefit roadblock, and Mayor Bill Bell announced public hearings and the October 13 comment deadline for the Durham-Orange Light Rail Draft EIS.

agenda_items.title: New Police Headquarters Site Alternatives and Carpenter Chevrolet Building Preservation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resuming after an omitted digest segment, Council debated architectural schemes for the new police station site and whether to spend roughly $4 million preserving the Carpenter Chevrolet building. One member opposed investing $4 million given no private developer had offered to buy the building, while another speaker emphasized balancing historical context against competing capital needs and ensuring active, walkable street-front uses along Main Street. Council reached consensus for staff to perform an apples-to-apples comparison and return to the September 24 or early October work session.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / Consensus referral to work session

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: US 70 Self Storage Center (Z1400020)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff member Pat Young presented a rezoning of 7.55 acres on US 70 Highway to Light Industrial with a Development Plan (IL(D)) for a self-storage center, including US 70 right-of-way dedication, land reservation for a future Page Road extension, a >4-foot fence, and a newly proffered commitment requiring a recorded permanent access easement prior to building permit or certificate of occupancy; the Planning Commission had recommended denial 1-10 on April 14 while staff recommended approval. Council Member Don Moffitt noted that the recorded easement resolved his primary access concern despite hesitation over splitting an existing development plan, and Council approved the rezoning 5-2 with Diane Catotti and Eddie Davis voting no, followed by a 7-0 consistency statement.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 5-2 (Ayes: Bell, Cole-McFadden, Brown, Schewel, Moffitt; Nays: Catotti, Davis); Consistency Statement 7-0

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments and Closing Discussion on Community Violence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk reported ballot appointment results: Barry Burch (7 votes) and Matthew McCarrihan (5 votes) to the Citizens Advisory Committee, and Andrew Hudson (4 votes) to the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission. Council Member Eddie Davis then initiated a closing discussion on local violence, emphasizing that addressing gun violence requires broader societal, family, and community engagement beyond policing alone.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Clerk reported ballot appointments (Burch: 7, McCarrihan: 5, Hudson: 4)

votes.item_title: Zoning Map Change: US 70 Self Storage Center (Z1400020)
votes.notes: Planning Commission recommended denial 1-10 on April 14, 2015; staff recommended approval with proffered access easement commitment.
votes.discussion_detail: Pat Young presented Z1400020 to rezone 7.55 acres on US 70 to IL(D) for a self-storage center despite a 1-10 denial recommendation from the Planning Commission. After the applicant added a commitment to record a permanent access easement prior to building permit or certificate of occupancy, Council Member Don Moffitt seconded the approval motion and voiced reluctant support, and Council passed the rezoning 5-2 with Diane Catotti and Eddie Davis voting no.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for US 70 Self Storage Center (Z1400020)
votes.discussion_detail: Following the 5-2 approval of the US 70 Self Storage Center rezoning, Council voted unanimously 7-0 to adopt the statutory consistency statement.

disagreements.issue: US 70 Self Storage Center Rezoning (Z1400020)
disagreements.summary: Council voted 5-2 to approve rezoning 7.55 acres on US 70 Highway to IL(D) for a self-storage facility despite a 1-10 Planning Commission denial recommendation. Mayor Bill Bell, Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden, Eugene Brown, Steve Schewel, and Don Moffitt voted in favor after the applicant proffered a permanent access easement covenant, while Diane Catotti and Eddie Davis voted no.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the US 70 Self Storage Center rezoning with the revised access easement commitment
side_a_arguments: Staff determined the proposal complied with UDO and policy provisions, including US 70 right-of-way dedication and Page Road reservation.
The applicant's newly proffered covenant requiring a recorded permanent access easement prior to building permit or certificate of occupancy addressed key access concerns (cited by Don Moffitt).
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose rezoning 7.55 acres to IL(D) for a self-storage facility
side_b_arguments: Voted no on the rezoning following a 1-10 Planning Commission denial recommendation (Don Moffitt also noted discomfort with severing half of an existing site development plan before ultimately voting yes).
disagreements.resolution: Passed 5-2

disagreements.issue: Carpenter Chevrolet Building Preservation at New Police Headquarters Site
disagreements.summary: Council debated whether to spend an estimated $4 million to preserve the historic Carpenter Chevrolet building as part of the new police headquarters design along Fayetteville/Main Street, weighing historic preservation against capital budget constraints and street-level activation.
disagreements.side_a_position: Oppose spending $4 million to preserve the Carpenter Chevrolet building
side_a_arguments: Spending $4 million on the structure was not justified relative to the building's assessed value and other capital needs.
No private developer had ever offered to purchase the building alone prior to city acquisition.

side_b_arguments: Historical context helps define Durham's identity rather than 'anywhere USA,' and at least one developer had expressed prior interest in the site.

meetings.title: Durham City Council August 17, 2015
meetings.executive_summary: With all seven members present, the Durham City Council added a resolution opposing state redistribution of local sales tax as priority Item 24 (7-0) and unanimously approved the consent agenda (7-0), including a five-year City-County inspections interlocal renewal, Morreene Road Apartments financing approval, three bicycle/pedestrian grant agreements, a 3810 Page Road condemnation for the Southeast Pressure Zone, and towing fee revisions. Council debated Item 6, a $201,000 Phase 1 consulting contract with Enterprise Community Partners, Inc. to design an affordable housing strategy—clashing over its five-month timeline versus 90 days and targeting 60–80% AMI versus under 60% AMI—before an omitted transcript gap. Council subsequently passed an unidentified planning item (7-0), adopted preliminary and final resolutions ordering street completions in Ravenstone and Stonehill Estates (7-0) with 10-year, zero-interest assessments averaging $22.51 and $21.09 monthly, passed Item 24 opposing sales tax redistribution (7-0), and approved two excused absence requests (7-0).

agenda_items.title: Priority Item 24 Addition and Consent Agenda Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield requested adding supplemental Item 24 (a resolution opposing local sales tax redistribution) as a priority item, which Council approved 7-0. Council then unanimously adopted the consent agenda (7-0), covering the June 2015 Grants Management audit, a five-year City-County inspections interlocal agreement renewal, Housing Authority financing approval for Morreene Road Apartments, bike/pedestrian grant agreements on Carpenter Fletcher, Cornwallis, and Hillandale Roads, a 3810 Page Road utility condemnation, workforce grant amendments, and towing fee revisions.

agenda_items.title: Consulting Contract with Enterprise Community Partners, Inc. ($201,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community Development Director Reginald Johnson presented a $201,000 Phase 1 technical assistance contract with Enterprise Community Partners, Inc. to design an affordable housing program, noting work-session concerns over whether funds should target 60–80% AMI or follow Council's transit corridor resolution targeting 15% affordable units below 60% AMI. Council members disagreed over whether the five-month timeline was unnecessarily slow compared to 90 days or warranted to design sound targeting and monitoring before the digest omitted the subsequent portion.

agenda_items.title: Planning / Policy Implementation Public Hearing Item

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Ordering Completion of Streets in Ravenstone and Stonehill Estates

Residents James O. Williams, Gwen Silver, and another homeowner raised concerns about raised manhole covers, construction delays, lack of contractor bids, and property values, while Council Member Don Moffitt urged expediting road completion and Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden asked about using excess stormwater funds in a future separate hearing. agenda_items.title: Resolution Opposing Local Sales Tax Redistribution and Excused Absences

meetings.title: Durham City Council August 3, 2015
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council opened its August 3, 2015 meeting with a National Night Out proclamation and addressed complaints from unpaid workers on the incentivized Residence Inn project at the Old McPherson Hospital site, with staff and the City Attorney explaining that the dispute lay with a subcontractor and required formal contract or mechanic's-lien resolution rather than city mediation. Council unanimously voted 7-0 to accept the City Clerk's priority item invalidating a protest petition on Item 39 after a signature withdrawal, and unanimously passed 7-0 a Unified Development Ordinance text amendment clarifying permissible-by-right encroachments in 10-foot riparian buffer setbacks and updating lot-of-record references to include Wake and Orange counties. Council also held a public hearing on raising the Private Drainage Assistance Program cap from $20,000 to $25,000 and debated Mayor Bill Bell's proposal to accelerate a downtown and transit-corridor affordable housing rental assistance program targeting 60% to 80% AMI households alongside hiring an affordable housing consultant.

agenda_items.title: National Night Out Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell read a proclamation declaring Tuesday, August 4, 2015 as the 32nd annual National Night Out against crime in Durham, recognizing more than 100 registered neighborhoods and partner law enforcement agencies including Durham Police, NCCU Police, Duke Police, and the Durham County Sheriff's Office. Public Affairs Manager Will accepted the proclamation on behalf of Chief Lopez and the Police Department.

agenda_items.title: Unpaid Subcontractor Dispute on Residence Inn (Old McPherson Hospital) Project
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Eugene Brown noted that while the city provided a $500,000 historic facade incentive for the Residence Inn project, council cannot act as a direct negotiator between workers and contractors. City Manager Tom Bonfield and City Attorney Patrick Baker reported that the Office of Economic and Workforce Development investigated and determined the nonpayment dispute involves a subcontractor, advising affected workers to pursue formal contract dispute resolution, mechanic's liens, or the Department of Labor since the city lacks privity of contract.

agenda_items.title: Mayor Bell's Downtown/Transit Affordable Housing Proposal and Youth Recognition Event
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell previewed a proposal he emailed to council, the City Manager, and the City Attorney for a downtown and half-mile transit-stop rental assistance program for low-to-moderate income families, noting it would be discussed under staff's incentive item and at the Thursday work session. He also announced an August 7 recognition event at the Durham Bulls Athletic Park for active local youth.

agenda_items.title: City Clerk Priority Item: Item 39 Zoning Map Change Protest Petition Ruled Invalid
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk reported that on Item 39 (zoning map change), a protest petition had been ruled invalid due to the withdrawal of a signature. Council moved, seconded, and voted unanimously to accept the City Clerk's priority item.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Reading (Public Works, Utilities, Leases, and Contracts)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read consent agenda items including Item 13 (Southside Homeownership Phase One architectural and engineering services), Item 14 (NC 751 and NC 54 sidewalk construction grant), Item 15 (Jordan Lake Partnership addendum), Item 16 (FY 2015-16 Water and Sewer fee schedule correction), Item 23 (Museum of Durham History lease at 521 W. Morgan Street), and ordinances on private driveway pipes and software licensing. The middle portion of the consent vote and intervening items was omitted in the transcript digest.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / No vote recorded in excerpt

agenda_items.title: Unified Development Ordinance Text Amendment: Riparian Buffer No-Build Setback and Lot of Record Definition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented two minor UDO amendments: allowing encroachments already permissible by right under state law and the UDO within the 10-foot riparian buffer no-build setback without requiring Board of Adjustment variances, and expanding the definition of 'lot of record' beyond Durham County to reference Wake and Orange County Register of Deeds offices. The Planning Commission had recommended approval 11-1 on June 9, and council passed the amendment 7-0 after closing the public hearing with no speakers.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Private Drainage Assistance Cost-Sharing and Interest Rate Revisions (Sections 70-687 and 70-688)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dana Hornkohl of Public Works presented two City Code revisions to raise the city's contribution cap for private drainage assistance projects from $20,000 to $25,000—maintaining the 80% cost-share goal amid rising construction costs—and to establish an annual interest rate for property owners using installment payments. During the hearing, unpaid Residence Inn subcontractor speakers who had waited were addressed again by the City Attorney regarding their lack of direct contractual recourse with the city.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / Vote not captured in excerpt

agenda_items.title: Council Discussion on Downtown and Transit-Corridor Affordable Housing Rental Assistance Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell urged council not to wait for the forthcoming affordable housing consultant study before launching a targeted rental assistance program for families at 60% to 80% of area median income in downtown and within a half-mile of proposed transit stops. A council colleague supported taking immediate action while highlighting existing investments—including 80 subsidized units and 48 homeownership units at Southside, $500,000 for the Durham Housing Authority, 9% and 4% LIHTC deals with penny-for-housing funds, and extending affordability periods on expiring apartments—and Mayor Bell agreed to focus initially on downtown and refine boundaries at Thursday's work session.

votes.item_title: Acceptance of City Clerk Priority Item (Item 39 Protest Petition Ruled Invalid)
votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not named on the record.
votes.discussion_detail: After the City Manager and City Attorney reported no priority items, the City Clerk informed council that a protest petition on Item 39 (zoning map change) had been ruled invalid following the withdrawal of a signature. Council moved, seconded, and approved accepting the priority item 7-0.

votes.item_title: Unified Development Ordinance Text Amendment (Riparian Buffer Setback Encroachments and Lot of Record Definition)
votes.notes: Planning Commission previously recommended approval 11-1 on June 9. Exact UDO item number omitted due to middle transcript truncation.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning staff explained that the amendment eliminates an unintended barrier requiring Board of Adjustment variances for encroachments already allowed by right in riparian buffers and updates the 'lot of record' definition to include Wake and Orange counties. With no public speakers, council closed the public hearing and approved the text amendment 7-0.

meetings.title: Durham City Council June 24, 2015
meetings.executive_summary: At its June 24, 2015 special meeting, the Durham City Council confirmed four appointees to the Civilian Police Review Board by ballot and unanimously approved (7-0) a $500,000 funding request for the Durham Housing Authority and Development Ventures Incorporated to support public housing redevelopment. Council then passed a maximum $6 million, 15-year economic development incentive agreement with Wexford Science & Technology to redevelop the Chesterfield Building (exact numeric tally not stated in the transcript excerpt), overcoming criticism of the county's $2.6 million share and fiscal return questions. On Item 4, council passed a preliminary economic development incentive agreement of up to $5.25 million over 15 years with Longfellow Real Estate Partners for the Durham Innovation District by a 6-1 split vote—Ayes: Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Eugene Brown, Steve Schewel, Eddie Davis, and Don Moffitt; Nay: Diane Catotti—after debate over tax-revenue percentages, deferred occupancy thresholds, and public park access, followed by Catotti's announcement that she would not seek reelection.

agenda_items.title: Council Memorials and Affordable Housing Milestones
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Eddie Davis noted the recent passing of Lewis Cheek and former advisory committee member and council candidate Edward Quon. Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden reported attending the groundbreaking for Phase Two of Denson Apartments for veterans and a homeownership celebration at Southside, praising the city's visible affordable housing progress.

agenda_items.title: Confirmation of Civilian Police Review Board Members
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council cast paper ballots to confirm nominees to the Civilian Police Review Board as recommended by the City Manager. At the conclusion of the meeting, Mayor Bill Bell announced that council confirmed all four appointees.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (all four appointees confirmed by ballot)

agenda_items.title: Durham Housing Authority and Development Ventures Inc. $500,000 Funding Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community Development Director Reginald Johnson and Durham Housing Authority CEO Dallas Parks presented a $500,000 funding request to support completion, lease-up, operating, and tax-credit guarantees for DHA/DVI affordable housing redevelopments, including Morreene Road and units for formerly homeless residents. Council Member Steve Schewel strongly endorsed DHA's emergence as a developer, and Mayor Pro Tem Cole-McFadden's motion to approve—with Council Member Diane Catotti requesting a 250-to-300 minimum unit target in the contract—passed 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Economic Development Incentive Agreement with Wexford Science & Technology (Chesterfield Building)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Office of Economic and Workforce Development Director Kevin Dick presented a proposed $6 million city incentive over 15 years (alongside a $2.6 million county commitment over five years, historic and new markets tax credits, and private equity) for Wexford Science & Technology to adaptively reuse the former Chesterfield factory into lab and office space, conditioned on workforce, M/WBE, and nights/weekends parking commitments. Some council members criticized the county's contribution as 'puny and measly' and questioned the fiscal return, while Mayor Bell defended the county's constraints and warned the building would continue deteriorating without the deal before council voted to approve.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Preliminary Economic Development Incentive Agreement with Longfellow Real Estate Partners (Durham Innovation District)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Kevin Dick presented a preliminary incentive agreement not to exceed $5.25 million over 15 years (net present value roughly $3 million) with Longfellow Real Estate Partners to build Class A lab and office space in the Durham Innovation District, with Michelle Jameson speaking in support. Diane Catotti opposed the 70% tax-revenue share, the deferral of the 70% occupancy requirement until year three, and insufficient public parking and county participation, while Don Moffitt and Steve Schewel questioned whether the planned park would be truly public and worried about future phases seeking subsidies; the agreement passed 6-1 with Catotti voting no.

agenda_items.title: Council Member Diane Catotti Retirement Announcement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following the vote on Item 4, Council Member Diane Catotti announced that after 12 years on the City Council she had decided not to file for reelection the following month. She thanked her colleagues, staff, husband, and family while pledging to continue working hard through her remaining five months in office.

votes.item_title: Confirmation of Four Appointees to the Civilian Police Review Board
votes.notes: Conducted via written ballot; individual vote counts were not stated in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Council members completed paper ballots at 00:09:53 for nominees to the Civilian Police Review Board. At adjournment (01:34:50), Mayor Bill Bell announced that the City Council had confirmed all four appointees as recommended by the City Manager.

votes.item_title: Durham Housing Authority and Development Ventures Incorporated $500,000 Affordable Housing Funding Request
votes.notes: Seconder was not named on the record.
votes.discussion_detail: Community Development Director Reginald Johnson and DHA CEO Dallas Parks detailed how the $500,000 request covers guarantees needed for DHA's public housing redevelopment pipeline, including Morreene Road and units serving formerly homeless residents. Steve Schewel praised DHA's transition into a capable developer, Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden moved approval, and Diane Catotti asked staff to specify a 250-to-300 minimum unit commitment in the contract before the motion passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Economic Development Incentive Agreement with Wexford Science & Technology (Chesterfield Building)
votes.notes: Exact numeric vote tally was not spoken in the transcript excerpt ('It passes'), though Steve Schewel later referenced disagreeing with the Mayor on both this item and Item 4.
votes.discussion_detail: Staff recommended negotiating a $6 million, 15-year incentive for Wexford Science & Technology's adaptive reuse of the former Chesterfield factory alongside $2.6 million from Durham County. After debate over parking requirements, tax returns, and whether the county was contributing enough, Mayor Bell defended the deal as essential to prevent further deterioration of the historic building, and the motion passed.

votes.item_title: Preliminary Economic Development Incentive Agreement with Longfellow Real Estate Partners, LLC (Durham Innovation District)
votes.notes: Diane Catotti was explicitly identified on the record as the sole dissenting vote ('It passes six to one with Council Member Catotti voting no').
votes.discussion_detail: Staff presented an up-to-$5.25 million, 15-year incentive for Longfellow Real Estate Partners to construct speculative Class A lab and office space in the Durham Innovation District. Diane Catotti questioned deferring the 70% occupancy requirement until year three, objected to the 70% future tax-revenue share and low county contribution, and voted no; Don Moffitt questioned whether the proposed park would be genuinely public and Steve Schewel voiced concern about future phases seeking subsidies, though both joined the 6-1 majority.

disagreements.issue: Wexford Science & Technology (Chesterfield Building) $6M Incentive and County Contribution Share
disagreements.summary: Council members debated the fiscal return of the city's $6 million, 15-year incentive for Wexford Science & Technology's adaptive reuse of the Chesterfield Building and whether Durham County's $2.6 million contribution was adequate.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support the city incentive as a necessary partnership with the county to rescue and activate the deteriorating Chesterfield Building.
side_a_arguments: Adaptive reuse of the former factory into lab space is cost-prohibitive after multiple failed redevelopment attempts.
Durham County carries a much larger budget and school funding mandates and is not obligated to contribute, yet its $2.6 million makes the deal viable.
Without the agreement, the Chesterfield Building will remain an eyesore and continue to deteriorate, whereas completion generates long-term net revenues.
disagreements.side_b_position: Question the city's fiscal exposure and criticize Durham County's $2.6 million commitment as disproportionately small.
side_b_arguments: The county's $2.6 million contribution over five years is inadequate relative to the city's $6 million over 15 years and the parking deck arrangements.
The fiscal and tax return structure requires stricter scrutiny before committing millions in city incentives.
disagreements.resolution: Motion passed (exact numeric tally not stated in the transcript excerpt).

disagreements.issue: Longfellow Real Estate Partners (Durham Innovation District) $5.25M Preliminary Incentive Terms
disagreements.summary: Council debated the subsidy level, year-three occupancy threshold, public park language, public parking availability, and future-phase subsidy expectations for the Durham Innovation District incentive.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the preliminary incentive agreement to catalyze Class A lab and office development on underutilized downtown parcels.
side_a_arguments: The project creates needed Class A office and high-tech lab space, attracts high-wage jobs, and increases long-term property tax revenue.
Deferring the 70% occupancy threshold until the third payment year reflects the leasing timeline for speculative lab buildings.
Staff addressed closed-session concerns regarding the proposed public park and future-phase expectations.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose the incentive terms as overly generous to the developer with insufficient public return and county participation.
side_b_arguments: Rebating 70% of future tax revenues over 15 years is too high.
Deferring the 70% occupancy requirement until year three is overly generous given claimed market demand.
A higher percentage of parking should be open to the public and Durham County should contribute more.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 6-1 (Diane Catotti voting No; Don Moffitt and Steve Schewel voted Aye while flagging park-access and future-phase incentive concerns).

meetings.title: Durham City Council June 15, 2015
meetings.executive_summary: At its June 15, 2015 meeting, the Durham City Council issued proclamations for National Parks and Recreation Month and the 25th anniversary of the Americans with Disabilities Act before approving the consent agenda 7-0 (excluding seven pulled items, including Item 15, the FY 2015-16 Budget and CIP pulled by Steve Schewel for priority trails cost discussion). Following a middle truncation in the digest, council unanimously approved 7-0 a developer public hearing item, Street Closing SC140017 for a portion of Roney Street (539 Foster Street project), and a 42-day extension to Concord Hospitality's downtown historic incentive agreement. On pulled consent items, council heard public criticisms regarding Terracon testing at the new Police Headquarters Complex (Item 27), youth workforce contracts (Items 34-36), and lack of Black-owned business inclusion in downtown contracts (Item 37), and unanimously approved 7-0 Items 34, 35, 36, 37, and Item 53 (completing streets and stormwater infrastructure in Stone Hill Estates and Ravenstone).

agenda_items.title: National Parks and Recreation Month and 25th Anniversary of the ADA Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presented three ceremonial proclamations, including National Parks and Recreation Month to Parks and Recreation Director Rhonda Parker and a proclamation honoring the 25th anniversary of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). The proclamations highlighted the health, environmental, economic, and accessibility benefits of city parks, trails, and ADA compliance efforts.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval and Pulls (Including Item 15 FY 2015-16 Budget and CIP)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read through the consent agenda covering board reappointments, the FY 2016-2018 Strategic Plan, the TIGER Grant for the Duke Beltline Trail Master Plan, water/sewer and fiber contracts, and Google Fiber licensing. meetings.title: Durham City Council June 1, 2015
meetings.executive_summary: The June 1, 2015 Durham City Council meeting began with a recognition of Carrington Middle School musicians and a unanimous 7-0 vote accepting the City Clerk's priority item ruling a protest petition on Item 30 insufficient. Council then opened the public hearing on the proposed FY 2015-16 budget through its third annual E-Town Hall moderated by Ken Smith, addressing property tax rates and affordable housing, a nearly $3 million revenue loss from state repeal of business privilege license fees, youth employment, police body cameras, and $2.1 million in arts funding. Following a middle transcript gap, council engaged in a sharp late-night debate over an NCDOT resurfacing and lane-reconfiguration ('road diet') plan for Durham-Chapel Hill Boulevard opposed by corridor business owners; after an initial 5-2 vote on Don Moffitt's motion to approve staff's 3-lane restriping plan was reopened for clarification, council passed Eugene Brown's substitute-to-the-substitute motion 4-3—Ayes: Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Eugene Brown, and Eddie Davis; Nays: Diane Catotti, Don Moffitt, and Steve Schewel—to proceed with state-funded resurfacing while deferring the striping decision until later in June.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Carrington Middle School Musical Performance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell thanked Carrington Middle School students and their music director for performing in the City Hall lobby prior to the meeting. He praised their engagement and invited them to return in the future.

agenda_items.title: City Clerk Priority Item: Item 30 Zoning Map Change Protest Petition Ruled Insufficient
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following no priority items from the City Manager or City Attorney, the City Clerk reported that a protest petition filed on Item 30 (zoning map change) had been ruled insufficient. Council moved, seconded, and accepted the priority item 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Proposed FY 2015-16 Budget Public Hearing and Third Annual E-Town Hall Meeting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell opened the FY 2015-16 budget public hearing with a 45-minute E-Town Hall moderated by WRAL anchor Ken Smith featuring questions submitted online and on audience cards. Council members discussed keeping tax rates sufficient to fund affordable housing (Mayor Bell), replacing nearly $3 million lost from state elimination of business privilege license fees (Eugene Brown), year-round youth activities and private-sector jobs (Cora Cole-McFadden), funding police body cameras for all officers alongside federal grant applications (Eddie Davis), and $2.1 million in arts and cultural support (Don Moffitt).

agenda_items.title: Durham-Chapel Hill Boulevard NCDOT Resurfacing and Lane Reconfiguration (5 Lanes vs. 3 Lanes)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff explained that NCDOT's summer resurfacing contract prompted review of a restriping plan converting Durham-Chapel Hill Boulevard to three lanes with bike lanes and 21 parking spaces, while corridor business owners testified against lane reductions and requested speed enforcement and a Hope Valley Road signal instead. Council split over whether to adopt staff's 3-lane reconfiguration immediately or delay, briefly voting 5-2 on Don Moffitt's motion to adopt staff's plan before reopening for clarification; council then passed Eugene Brown's substitute-to-the-substitute motion 4-3 to accept NCDOT resurfacing now and decide striping later in June.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 4-3 (Ayes: Bell, Cole-McFadden, Brown, Davis; Nays: Catotti, Moffitt, Schewel)

votes.item_title: Acceptance of City Clerk Priority Item (Item 30 Protest Petition Ruled Insufficient)
votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not named on the record.
votes.discussion_detail: The City Clerk announced that a protest petition filed on Item 30 (zoning map change) had been ruled insufficient. Council moved, seconded, and unanimously accepted the priority item 7-0.

votes.item_title: Substitute-to-the-Substitute Motion: Proceed with NCDOT Resurfacing of Durham-Chapel Hill Boulevard and Defer Striping Decision
votes.notes: Earlier reopened 5-2 vote on Don Moffitt's substitute motion (with Mayor Bell voting no) was vacated/superseded upon reopening and adoption of Eugene Brown's substitute-to-the-substitute.
votes.discussion_detail: Following business-owner opposition to reducing Durham-Chapel Hill Boulevard from five lanes to three lanes, council first moved to delay for one two-week cycle, then voted 5-2 on a substitute motion by Don Moffitt to approve staff's 3-lane restriping plan before reopening that vote for procedural clarification. Council Member Eugene Brown then moved a substitute-to-the-substitute to accept NCDOT-funded resurfacing immediately and return by late June to decide the striping configuration; staff noted NCDOT would revert to existing 5-lane striping if council did not decide within six weeks, and the motion passed 4-3 with Diane Catotti, Don Moffitt, and Steve Schewel voting no.

disagreements.issue: Durham-Chapel Hill Boulevard Lane Reconfiguration (3-Lane Road Diet vs. 5-Lane Status Quo / Delay)
disagreements.summary: Council divided 4-3 over whether to adopt staff's proposed three-lane bike/parking reconfiguration immediately or accept NCDOT resurfacing while deferring the striping decision due to business-owner opposition.
disagreements.side_a_position: Proceed with NCDOT-funded resurfacing immediately and defer the striping decision until late June to allow further discussion with affected businesses.
side_a_arguments: Durham should not turn down state NCDOT resurfacing funding for a deteriorated corridor.
A large share of local business owners along the short corridor opposed the lane reduction and felt insufficiently consulted, signaling a communication breakdown.
The proposed plan adds only 21 parking spaces, and council still has until the end of June to finalize striping.
disagreements.side_b_position: Decide the striping configuration directly rather than adopting a convoluted deferral, with supporters of the 3-lane plan arguing delay jeopardizes safety and parking improvements.
side_b_arguments: Slowing traffic and adding bike lanes and parking makes pulling out of corridor restaurants and shops safer and will attract more customers.
Deferring to an unspecified later vote is procedurally convoluted and risks missing NCDOT's summer contract deadline or overloading the next 63-item agenda.
Council should vote directly up-or-down on the three-lane vs. five-lane striping rather than deferring.
disagreements.resolution: Eugene Brown's substitute-to-the-substitute motion to proceed with NCDOT resurfacing and revisit striping later passed 4-3 (Ayes: Bell, Cole-McFadden, Brown, Davis; Nays: Catotti, Moffitt, Schewel).

meetings.title: Proposed FY '15 - '16 Budget Presentation
meetings.executive_summary: This May 20, 2015 video is a standalone presentation recording of City Manager Tom Bonfield delivering General Business Item 19, the Proposed FY 2015-16 Budget and FY 2016-2021 Capital Improvement Plan, to the Durham City Council and public. Bonfield presented a $386.5 million total budget (down nearly 1%) and a $170.2 million General Fund budget (down nearly 3%) with no property tax rate increase (59.12 cents per $100 assessed value), offsetting over $2.9 million lost from the state's repeal of the business privilege license tax and establishing a dedicated tax allocation for solid waste while maintaining a projected 21% fund balance. Key spending priorities included $91.4 million for public safety with all sworn positions funded, $2 million for street paving, $500,000 for sidewalks, a continued half-cent tax for parks maintenance, a 3% water and sewer rate increase, an Open Government Portal, and public input through the June 1 E-Town Hall; no formal votes occurred on the budget presentation itself.

agenda_items.title: Proposed FY 2015-16 Budget and FY 2016-2021 Capital Improvement Plan Overview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following the tail end of a prior 7-0 consent vote, Mayor Bill Bell introduced General Business Item 19 for City Manager Tom Bonfield's formal budget presentation. Bonfield outlined a $386.5 million total budget and $170.2 million General Fund budget holding the tax rate flat at 59.12 cents, replacing over $2.9 million in repealed business privilege license revenue, creating a dedicated solid waste tax allocation, and using $1.7 million of fund balance while maintaining roughly 21% reserves.

agenda_items.title: Customer Service, Arts, Open Government Portal, and Neighborhood Initiatives
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Bonfield proposed a citywide customer service review, an additional Durham One Call representative, and a resident problem-reporting smartphone app. He also highlighted continued support for cultural festivals such as Full Frame, the American Dance Festival, and Art of Cool, a planned Durham Sports Commission partnership with the county and CVB, a new Open Government Portal launching the next month, and a mobile-friendly city website redesign.

agenda_items.title: Public Safety Funding Allocation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Bonfield reported that public safety accounts for $91.4 million of the proposed budget, with nearly 62% directed to law enforcement. While no new police officer or firefighter positions were added for FY 2015-16, all existing sworn positions remained fully funded alongside ongoing deployment reviews to plan for future personnel needs as Durham grows.

agenda_items.title: Infrastructure, Street Paving, Parks Maintenance, Utilities, and Capital Projects
agenda_items.discussion_summary: To address physical asset backlogs and resident survey priorities, the proposed budget increased deferred maintenance funding to $600,000, added $108,000 for asset management software, boosted street paving to $2 million alongside $500,000 for sidewalks, and continued the dedicated half-cent tax (~$1.2 million) for parks maintenance. It also proposed an average 3% water and sewer rate increase generating $2.9 million for line maintenance, no stormwater rate increase, and more than $12.9 million in capital projects.

agenda_items.title: Public Input Schedule and Mayor Bell's Closing Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Bonfield invited residents to submit budget feedback via email, social media, YouTube, and Durham One Call ahead of the June 1 E-Town Hall and thanked Budget and Management Services Director Bertha Johnson and department directors. Mayor Bill Bell commended the balanced, no-tax-increase proposal as a strong foundation for upcoming council budget deliberations.
