meetings.title: Durham City Council January 5, 2015
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council approved its consent agenda—including a resolution welcoming unaccompanied migrant children—and referred the Auto Park Center rezoning (Z1400011) back to staff, but split sharply over two major policy items. On a 3-4 vote, the council rejected adding the Durham County Sheriff's proposal to elevate stolen firearm offenses and impose a 72-month mandatory minimum to its 2015 legislative agenda before approving the remaining legislative package 6-0. After an extensive public hearing featuring residents from Parkwood, Eno Trace, and Green Street, council voted 5-1 (Council Member Eugene Brown dissenting) to rescind 11 previously ordered $5-per-foot petition sidewalk projects while pledging to revisit sidewalk funding in the budget process.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations for Dr. John Hope Franklin Centennial, Justice Sunday 2015, and National Mentoring Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell presented three proclamations honoring Dr. John Hope Franklin's centennial birthday, proclaiming January 18, 2015 as Justice Sunday (accepted by NCCU Professor Dr. John B. Wilson), and recognizing January 2015 as National Mentoring Month (accepted by Durham County Juvenile Crime Prevention Council Vice Chair DeWarren Langley and Thomas Leadership Mentoring Academy President Larry Thomas). Council Member Steve Schewel also recognized community members present in support of the consent-agenda resolution welcoming unaccompanied migrant children, and Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden received an excused absence to depart early for a citywide revival.

agenda_items.title: Referral of Zoning Map Change Auto Park Center (Z1400011) Back to Administration / Planning Department
agenda_items.discussion_summary: As a City Manager priority item, the manager reported that the applicant's attorney and design consultant for Auto Park Center (Z1400011) requested late that afternoon to refer the item back to the City-County Planning Department to address a site plan issue. Council referred the rezoning case back to administration for consideration at a later date.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Unaccompanied Migrant Children Resolution, Expedited Rezoning Z1400034, EV Charger License, Avondale Sidewalk, Street/DOT & Property Contracts)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved all remaining consent agenda items in a single vote, including board appointments to the Firefighters' Relief Fund, RDU Airport Authority, and Passenger Vehicle for Hire Commission, a resolution welcoming unaccompanied migrant children in Durham, an expedited hearing request for Southside East Phases 2 and 3 (Z1400034), a BrightField DC fast charger license in Parking Lot 32, Avondale Drive sidewalk construction, street acceptances, and several NCDOT and facility contracts.

agenda_items.title: 2015 Long Session Legislative Agenda and Sheriff's Stolen Firearms Penalty Enhancement Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Assistant to the City Manager Karmisha Wallace presented the 2015 Long Session Legislative Agenda, highlighting a separate request from the Durham County Sheriff to elevate larceny, sale, or receipt of stolen firearms from Class H to Class E felony and impose a 72-month mandatory minimum when another felony is committed with a stolen firearm. Criminal justice advocates opposed the enhancement as disruptive to NC's sentencing structure and ineffective, while the Sheriff and his legal advisor urged action amid rising gun violence and break-ins; council split 3-4 against including the Sheriff's item and then adopted the rest of the legislative agenda 6-0.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Sheriff proposal failed 3-4; Remainder of legislative agenda passed 6-0

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Resolution to Rescind 11 Previously Ordered Petition Sidewalks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Works Director Marvin Williams presented a resolution to rescind 11 previously ordered $5-per-front-foot petition sidewalk projects so council could transition to updated assessment rates ($35/foot for projects in the Durham Walks plan or full construction cost outside it). Residents from Parkwood, Eno Trace, and Green Street spoke about pedestrian hazards, flawed consultant scoring, and underfunded sidewalk budgets, while one Green Street homeowner favored rescission; council passed the rescission 5-1 with Council Member Eugene Brown opposed.

votes.item_title: Excused Absence Request for Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden
votes.notes: Cole-McFadden remained through the 3-4 legislative agenda vote on the Sheriff's proposal before departing for Union Baptist Church.
votes.discussion_detail: During council announcements, Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden congratulated the Durham Ministerial Alliance on its Emancipation Proclamation service and citywide revival beginning that evening at Union Baptist Church. Explaining her desire to join the city's spiritual leaders in corporate prayer, she requested an excused absence to leave the meeting around 7:45 p.m. Council Member Eddie Davis moved to grant the excused absence, Council Member Diane Catotti seconded, and the motion passed 7-0 (though Cole-McFadden later stayed through the Sheriff's legislative proposal vote before departing).

votes.item_title: Refer Zoning Map Change Auto Park Center (Z1400011) Back to Administration / City-County Planning Department
votes.notes: City Manager priority item; applicant's attorney and design consultant requested referral to address a site plan issue.
votes.discussion_detail: During priority items, the City Manager informed council that the applicant's attorney and design consultant for Item 23, Zoning Map Change Auto Park Center (Z1400011), contacted the city late that afternoon requesting that the case be referred back to the City-County Planning Department to address a site plan issue. No members of council objected or requested discussion on the deferral. Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden moved the referral, Council Member Don Moffitt seconded (with Diane Catotti also initially referenced), and the motion passed unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Include Durham County Sheriff's Stolen Firearms Felony Enhancement Proposal in 2015 Long Session Legislative Agenda
votes.notes: Electronic board tally announced as 3 yeses and 4 noes without clerk reading every individual member name aloud; Cole-McFadden (mover), Brown (seconder, confirmed Yes), and Bell spoke in support, while Schewel, Moffitt, and Davis argued against and Catotti formed the fourth Nay.
votes.discussion_detail: Senior Assistant to the City Manager Karmisha Wallace explained that the Sheriff requested council support—without requiring city lobbying—to elevate larceny, sale, or receipt of stolen firearms from a Class H to a Class E felony and establish a 72-month mandatory minimum sentence for felonies committed with a stolen firearm. Public speakers Leo Rupert (Carolina Justice Policy Center), Marcia Owen (Religious Coalition for a Nonviolent Durham), and Prof. George Wilson (NCCU) opposed the proposal as counterproductive, arguing it equates property theft with violent crimes against persons, imposes ~$175,000 incarceration costs per sentence without deterrence evidence, and worsens mass incarceration compared to safe-storage education or gun legislation. Sheriff Mike Andrews and legal advisor Curtis Massey arrived mid-debate to argue that rising residential break-ins (30-40% increase, including stolen gun safes) and street gun violence justify Class E classification alongside other hazard offenses, with Mayor Bell, Mayor Pro Tem Cole-McFadden, and Council Member Brown voicing support for sending a strong anti-violence message. However, Council Members Steve Schewel, Don Moffitt, and Eddie Davis criticized the lack of consultation with the NC Sentencing Commission, the absence of crime-reduction projections, and the removal of judicial discretion through a six-year mandatory minimum, and Schewel requested an up-or-down vote on isolating the Sheriff's request, which failed 3-4.

votes.item_title: Adopt 2015 Long Session Legislative Agenda (Excluding Sheriff's Stolen Firearms Proposal)
votes.notes: Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden departed under her previously approved excused absence immediately after the 3-4 vote on the Sheriff's proposal, leaving six members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately after the council voted 3-4 against adding the Sheriff's stolen firearms proposal to the legislative package, Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden departed for the Union Baptist Church revival under her previously granted excused absence. Council Member Steve Schewel thanked the Sheriff for his daily public safety work, and Mayor Bell was about to move to Item 22 when a council member noted they still needed to vote on the underlying 2015 Long Session Legislative Agenda itself. A motion to adopt the remainder of the legislative agenda was made, seconded, and approved unanimously 6-0 by the remaining members.

votes.item_title: Resolution Rescinding 11 Previously Ordered Petition Sidewalk Projects (Item 22)
votes.notes: Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden was absent (excused); Council Member Eugene Brown voted No. Clarified post-vote that council adopted the base rescission recommendation without yet selecting any of staff's follow-up budget alternatives.
votes.discussion_detail: Public Works Director Marvin Williams presented the proposal to rescind 11 previously ordered $5-per-front-foot sidewalk petitions so council could clear an unfunded backlog and require new petitions to pay $35 per foot (for projects in the Durham Walks plan) or full construction cost (~$55 per foot) outside it. During the public hearing, Parkwood Association President Bill Mitchell (citing Grandale and Sedgwick Road safety and disputed consultant scoring), Eno Trace residents Wallace Lam and Jesse Vassel (describing blind hills and Lam's broken arm from walking without sidewalks), and Green Street petition owner Maria Pajowski (arguing the $200,000 sidewalk budget versus $14 million in needs was a false choice) urged council not to rescind, while Green Street resident Ron De Silva supported rescission over tree and privacy impacts. Council Member Diane Catotti moved rescission to prioritize scarce funds via the Durham Walks plan, backed by Steve Schewel and Don Moffitt (who entered an opposing email from Deidre Murphy on University Drive into the record while noting it was misleading to keep 7-to-8-year-old unfunded petitions on the books). Council Member Eugene Brown cast the sole dissent in the 5-1 vote, faulting consultant scoring that gave zero points to Parkwood's HOA park and arguing Durham must better fund neighborhood sidewalk connectivity.

disagreements.issue: Inclusion of Sheriff's Stolen Firearms Felony Elevation and 72-Month Mandatory Minimum in 2015 Legislative Agenda
disagreements.summary: Council divided 3-4 over whether to endorse the Durham County Sheriff's proposal asking the General Assembly to elevate stolen firearm offenses from Class H to Class E felony and impose a mandatory 72-month minimum prison term when a stolen firearm is used in another felony.
disagreements.side_a_position: Endorse the Sheriff's stolen firearm penalty enhancement in the city's 2015 legislative package to deter gun thefts and violence.
side_a_arguments: Stolen firearms and residential burglaries (up 30-40%, including stolen gun safes) feed street-level gun violence, aggravated assaults, and homicides in Durham.
Stealing a firearm is an intentional act whose purpose is typically resale or criminal use, warranting tougher Class E felony status and incapacitation.
Supporting the Sheriff sends a clear community message that gun violence is intolerable.
disagreements.side_b_position: Decline to add the Sheriff's sentencing enhancement to the city's legislative agenda.
side_b_arguments: Elevating property theft of a firearm to Class E disrupts North Carolina's structured sentencing grid by equating theft with violent crimes against persons.
A mandatory 72-month minimum eliminates judicial discretion contrary to national sentencing reform trends and carries high incarceration costs without evidence of deterrence.
The Sheriff had not consulted the NC Sentencing Commission, lacked crime-reduction projections, and existing 2013 firearm sentencing enhancements have not yet been evaluated.
disagreements.resolution: Motion to add the Sheriff's proposal to the legislative agenda failed 3-4; the remaining 2015 legislative agenda was then approved 6-0.

disagreements.issue: Rescission of 11 Previously Ordered $5/Foot Petition Sidewalk Projects
disagreements.summary: Following resident testimony over pedestrian safety and consultant scoring fairness, council split 5-1 on rescinding 11 older petition sidewalk orders to transition toward the Durham Walks prioritization framework and higher $35/foot petitioner assessments.
disagreements.side_a_position: Rescind the 11 older petition orders now and revisit sidewalk funding and prioritization alternatives during the upcoming budget process.
side_a_arguments: Leaving petitions approved 7-8 years ago on the active list when they lack funding is misleading to residents.
Very limited sidewalk funds should be directed through the Durham Walks priority plan to maximize safety, school proximity, and overall connectivity.
Five of the 11 corridors remain in the Durham Walks plan and can be re-petitioned at $35/foot alongside future budget discussions.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose rescinding the previously ordered neighborhood petition sidewalks.
side_b_arguments: Consultant scoring criteria unfairly penalized neighborhood projects such as Sedgwick Road in Parkwood because the adjacent park is HOA-owned rather than city-owned and the route connects to an existing school sidewalk rather than fronting the school directly.
Durham is already 'sidewalk poor' and should prioritize intra-neighborhood connectivity and citizen volunteer efforts rather than canceling approved projects.
disagreements.resolution: Resolution rescinding the 11 petition sidewalk projects passed 5-1 (Cole-McFadden excused absent), with staff directed to bring sidewalk funding and Durham Walks options back during the FY2015-16 budget process.

meetings.title: Durham City Council December 15, 2014
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council unanimously adopted a special resolution supporting the nomination of Durham-raised Loretta Lynch as U.S. Attorney General, presented proclamations for the 40th anniversary of the Safe Drinking Water Act and Human Rights and Bill of Rights Day, and approved the 18-item consent agenda. Council members also discussed recent local protests over the Michael Brown and Eric Garner grand jury decisions, praising Durham Police Department professionalism while emphasizing existing protest conduct rules. In public hearings, the Council unanimously approved consolidated annexations and initial zonings for the 117.1-acre Ravenstone Extension and the 3.11-acre Massey's Chapel United Methodist Church, as well as the closing of a segment of Elder Street adjacent to Duke University.

agenda_items.title: 40th Anniversary of the Safe Drinking Water Act Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presented a proclamation recognizing December 17 as the 40th anniversary of the federal Safe Drinking Water Act of 1974. Water Management Director Don Greeley accepted the proclamation on behalf of his more than 300 employees, highlighting Durham's long-standing commitment to water quality and capital planning.

agenda_items.title: Human Rights and Bill of Rights Day Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell proclaimed December 15, 2014 as Human Rights and Bill of Rights Day in Durham, reaffirming Resolution 9046 protecting civil rights regardless of immigration status, welcoming Central American children and adolescents, and noting Durham's recent policy requiring written consent for vehicle searches. Joan Walsh of the Bill of Rights Defense Committee thanked Council Member Steve Schewel and the Council for advancing civil rights protections.

agenda_items.title: Resolution in Support of Loretta Lynch's Nomination for U.S. Attorney General
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell and City Attorney Patrick Baker presented a resolution endorsing the nomination of Loretta Lynch, who grew up in Durham and attended Durham Public Schools, to serve as the 83rd U.S. Attorney General. Lynch's father, Reverend Lorenzo A. Lynch, thanked the Council for its support ahead of U.S. Senate Judiciary Committee hearings.

agenda_items.title: Council Announcements on Profiling Legislation and Recent Protest Marches
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Eddie Davis reported attending Representative Rodney Moore's press conference announcing a proposed state bill to prohibit discriminatory profiling. Mayor Bell and Council Members Don Moffitt and Eugene Brown then discussed a Saturday night protest march stemming from the Michael Brown and Eric Garner decisions that resulted in 11 arrests near Swift Avenue and NC 147, commending DPD restraint and noting that the city's protest conduct rules should be shared publicly.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Adoption (Items 1-18)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: No council members or members of the public requested to pull any item from the 18-item consent agenda. Items included Southside Revitalization Phase II contracts, a Pulte Home Corporation land donation for Fire Station 17, City Hall Annex funding, Durham Convention Center agreements with the County and Global Spectrum, an EPA Brownfields assessment grant for Northeast Central Durham, and utility/engineering contracts.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation and Initial Zoning: Ravenstone Extension (BDG1400005)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a voluntary annexation, utility extension agreement, and initial zoning request by Lennar Carolinas LLC for 117.1 acres along Sherron Road to allow up to 230 single-family homes under RR and F/J-B zoning. Nearby residents voiced concerns over inadequate notice, speeding on Hidden Brook Drive, stormwater runoff, wildlife, and road capacity, while staff and Council Member Don Moffitt noted the initial zoning represented a downzoning from county RS-20 and that detailed stormwater and traffic reviews occur at the site plan stage.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation and Initial Zoning: Massey's Chapel (BDG1400009)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a utility extension agreement, contiguous annexation, and initial RR(F/J-B) zoning request for 3.11 acres off Fayetteville Road occupied by Massey's Chapel United Methodist Church, with no expansion proposed. No members of the public spoke during the hearing.

agenda_items.title: Street Closing: Elder Street (SC1400011)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pat Young of the Planning Department presented an application by Triangle Land Surveyors on behalf of Duke University to close a 430.43-linear-foot segment of Elder Street surrounded entirely by Duke University property. Staff reported no service delivery objections and recommended approval; no public speakers appeared.

votes.item_title: Resolution in Support of the Nomination of Loretta Lynch as U.S. Attorney General
votes.notes: Mayor Bell indicated copies of the resolution would be sent to the U.S. Senate Judiciary Committee, North Carolina's two U.S. Senators, and Reverend Lorenzo Lynch's family.
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Bill Bell introduced the resolution honoring Loretta Lynch, who was raised in Durham and educated in Durham Public Schools before President Barack Obama nominated her on November 8, 2014 to succeed Eric Holder as the 83rd U.S. Attorney General. City Attorney Patrick Baker read the full resolution detailing Lynch's education at W.G. Pearson Elementary, Whitted Junior High, Durham High School, Harvard University, and Harvard Law School, as well as her federal prosecutorial career in the Eastern District of North Carolina and Eastern District of New York. Reverend Lorenzo A. Lynch thanked the Council for its support as his daughter prepared for U.S. Senate Judiciary Committee confirmation hearings. Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden moved passage, seconded by Council Member Steve Schewel, and the Council adopted the resolution unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Consolidated Annexation, Utility Extension, and Initial Zoning: Ravenstone Extension (BDG1400005)
votes.notes: Applies RR and F/J-B initial zoning to 117.1 acres along Sherron Road.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning staff presented Lennar Carolinas LLC's application for contiguous annexation, utility extension, and initial RR(F/J-B) zoning on 117.1 acres along Sherron Road for up to 230 single-family homes, noting a 12-0 Planning Commission recommendation. Council Member Steve Schewel clarified with Water Management Director Don Greeley that an attachment memo misprinted outside-city rates instead of inside-city rates. Three neighboring residents—Gina Scarcella, Brian, and Chastity Martin—testified about not receiving notices and raised alarms regarding 65 mph speeding on Hidden Brook Drive, stormwater runoff, wildlife habitat, and Sherron Road congestion. Staff explained that notices were mailed within 600 feet and that stormwater, road access, and environmental protections would be enforced during subsequent site plan review, while Council Member Don Moffitt emphasized that the proposed RR zoning reduced allowable density compared to the property's existing county RS-20 zoning; Council approved the item 7-0.

votes.item_title: Consistency Statement: Ravenstone Extension (BDG1400005)
votes.notes: Statutory consistency statement accompanying BDG1400005.
votes.discussion_detail: Following approval of the Ravenstone Extension annexation and initial zoning, Mayor Bell called for the statutory statement of consistency with the Comprehensive Plan. Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden moved approval of the consistency statement, seconded by Council Member Eddie Davis. Council Member Don Moffitt also reiterated to the attending neighbors that Planning staff would follow up with them directly with contact information for the assigned planner so they could monitor the upcoming site plan review. The consistency statement passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Consolidated Annexation, Utility Extension, and Initial Zoning: Massey's Chapel (BDG1400009)
votes.notes: Applies initial RR(F/J-B) zoning to 3.11 acres for Massey's Chapel United Methodist Church off Fayetteville Road.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning staff presented case BDG1400009 for Massey's Chapel United Methodist Church, requesting a utility extension agreement, contiguous annexation, and initial zoning of Rural Residential with the Falls/Jordan Watershed Protection Overlay B for two parcels totaling 3.11 acres off Fayetteville Road. Staff noted the annexation would connect an existing satellite annexation to the south, no expansion of the existing place of worship was proposed, and the initial zoning matched the existing county zoning as the least intense district available. No council questions or public comments were offered during the public hearing. Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden moved approval, seconded by Council Member Eugene Brown, and the motion passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Consistency Statement: Massey's Chapel (BDG1400009)
votes.notes: Statutory consistency statement accompanying BDG1400009.
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately following the annexation and initial zoning vote for Massey's Chapel, the Council took up the required statement of consistency with the Comprehensive Plan. Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden moved approval, seconded by Council Member Eugene Brown. Without further discussion, the Council approved the consistency statement 7-0.

votes.item_title: Street Closing: Elder Street (SC1400011)
votes.notes: Closes 430.43 linear feet of Elder Street right-of-way surrounded by Duke University property.
votes.discussion_detail: Pat Young of the Planning Department presented case SC1400011, an application filed by Ron Carpenter of Triangle Land Surveyors to close a 430.43-linear-foot segment of Elder Street bordered on both sides by Duke University property in the Duke Hospital Compact Neighborhood Tier. Staff reported that partner and service delivery agencies raised no concerns and recommended approval so the right-of-way could be recombined with adjacent Duke parcels. No council members or members of the public spoke on the item. Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden moved approval, seconded by Council Member Eugene Brown, and the street closing passed 7-0.

meetings.title: Durham City Council December 1, 2014
meetings.executive_summary: In a three-and-a-half-hour meeting dominated by land-use and affordable housing debates, the Durham City Council rejected (1-6) a private UDO text amendment to allow unipole wireless towers administratively, opting to await comprehensive wireless facility revisions. Council then split 5-2 to approve the Erwin Terrace at LaSalle Street Comprehensive Plan amendment expanding the Compact Neighborhood Tier despite extensive public testimony from affordable housing advocates seeking a 15% set-aside, before voting 7-0 to approve the companion rezoning after the developer proffered $25,000 for the city's affordable housing toolbox, $23,000 for Durham Public Schools, and an 18-month hold on redeveloping Poplar Manor. Council also approved rezonings for Grandin Trace (6-1) and a Waffle House on NC 55 (6-1), plus pulled consent items on roadside memorials and a Byrne criminal justice grant.

agenda_items.title: Announcement on Fayetteville Street Resurfacing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell announced that NCDOT had finally begun resurfacing Fayetteville Street near North Carolina Central University from NC 147 toward Cornwallis Road, with completion expected by year-end. He noted that although the city had resurfaced many local streets via voter-approved bonds, Fayetteville Street remained under state maintenance jurisdiction.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Adoption (excluding pulled Items 7 and 13)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read the Consent Agenda, covering minutes, appointments, strategic plan and take-home vehicle performance audits, the FY2014 CAFR, the FY15-16 budget schedule, the 2015 Council calendar, NC 55/Alston Avenue widening agreement, cemetery design amendments, DOT sign shop land acquisition, and sidewalk hearing notices. Items 7 and 13 were pulled for separate discussion.

agenda_items.title: UDO Text Amendment: Unipole Freestanding Wireless Communications Facilities (TC1400004)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Morningstar Law Group attorney Patrick Byker presented a private text amendment for Durham Tower LLC to allow unipoles ('slick sticks') administratively in non-residential districts ahead of a broader citywide wireless ordinance overhaul (TC120013), citing a planned tower near Durham Tech. Planning staff preferred incorporating it into TC120013, and neighborhood speakers Dolly and Mel Fahrenbacher urged Council to wait and preserve public hearing protections, leading a 6-1 majority to reject the amendment.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment: Erwin Terrace at LaSalle Street (A130010)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Erwin Terrace LLC requested changing 19.64 acres at Erwin Road and LaSalle Street from Urban Tier to Compact Neighborhood Tier adjacent to a planned light rail station, proffering $25,000 toward the city's affordable housing toolbox and a 12-month pause on redeveloping Poplar Manor. Advocates from Durham CAN, People's Alliance, and Durham Community Land Trustees urged delaying approval until 15% affordable housing was secured, while a 5-2 Council majority approved the tier change citing existing 79.5% affordability within a half-mile, transit density needs, and state-law bans on mandatory inclusionary zoning.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Erwin Terrace at LaSalle Street (Z130031)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: In the companion rezoning on 9.86 acres to Mixed Use with Development Plan under Compact Neighborhood standards (up to 322 residential units and 498,000 sq ft of office, commercial, and civic space), the developer expanded its Poplar Manor redevelopment moratorium to 18 months, reaffirmed the $25,000 affordable housing planning contribution, and committed $23,000 ($500 per projected student) to Durham Public Schools. With those proffers added and the tier change already approved, Council unanimously approved the rezoning.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Grandin Trace (Z130035)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Regent Development sought to rezone 20.05 acres between Herndon Road and Grandale Drive to RR(D) and PDR 3.322 for up to 53-54 single-family homes. Neighbor George Bryan requested a left-turn lane at Grandale Drive and Barbee Road, while Mayor Bell questioned tree removal along Grandale and Council Member Don Moffitt objected that all traffic exited onto Grandale without Herndon Road access.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Waffle House NC 55 Highway (Z140019)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a 1.5-acre rezoning at 4203 NC 55 Highway from Office Institutional to Commercial Neighborhood for a Waffle House restaurant. Nearby resident Sharon Maddox raised concerns over severe June 2013 flooding on Henry Place and traffic on Carpenter Fletcher Road; Mayor Bell cited ongoing flooding concerns in voting no, while Council Member Don Moffitt noted modern Falls/Jordan Lake stormwater detention standards would apply.

agenda_items.title: Landlord's Certificate Approval for Shannon SP Associates LP
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council considered a supplemental item approving a City of Durham landlord's certificate for tenant Shannon SP Associates Limited Partnership without debate.

agenda_items.title: Policy on Memorials on City Property or Right-of-Way
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Victoria Peterson pulled Item 7 to question why the proposed 45-day temporary roadside memorial policy referred to memorials as 'unauthorized' and argued 45 days was too short. Deputy City Manager Bo Ferguson and City Attorney Patrick Baker clarified the policy established uniform guidelines for spontaneous roadside memorials without automatically authorizing every placement.

agenda_items.title: FY 2014 Byrne Criminal Justice Innovation Program Planning Grant Award
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson pulled Item 13 to ask why grant research funds went to UNC-Greensboro rather than North Carolina Central University or local youth anti-crime programs. Police official Ed Sarvis explained the U.S. Attorney's Office referred UNCG for specialized census-tract research without an RFP, and Council Member Don Moffitt confirmed no local city dollars were committed while participation preserved eligibility for a $1 million implementation grant.

votes.item_title: Approval of Consent Agenda (Items 1-14, excluding Items 7 and 13)
votes.notes: Items 7 and 13 were pulled for separate consideration.
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Bell read the 14-item Consent Agenda, which included performance audit reports on the Citywide Strategic Plan and Take-Home Vehicles, the FY2014 Comprehensive Annual Financial Report, the FY15-16 budget development schedule, the 2015 Council meeting calendar, an NCDOT municipal agreement for NC 55/Alston Avenue widening, cemetery design amendments, property acquisition for the DOT sign and signal shop, and setting a public hearing on 11 petitioned sidewalk projects. Items 7 (roadside memorials policy) and 13 (Byrne Criminal Justice grant) were pulled for public comment. Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden moved approval of the remaining consent items, seconded by Council Member Eugene Brown, and the motion passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: UDO Text Amendment: Unipole Freestanding Wireless Communications Facilities (TC1400004)
votes.notes: At 03:28:42, the City Clerk corrected the record to confirm Mayor Pro Tempore Cole-McFadden voted No rather than Yes.
votes.discussion_detail: Michael Stock of the Planning Department presented TC1400004, a privately initiated text amendment by Morningstar Law Group for Durham Tower LLC to allow unipoles ('slick sticks') administratively in non-residential districts, noting that staff preferred folding the change into the comprehensive wireless facility overhaul (TC120013) due in late winter or early spring. Applicant attorney Patrick Byker and partner Matthew Danielson argued the amendment was urgently needed to place a visually unobtrusive tower near Durham Tech without resorting to a monopine, while Dolly and Mel Fahrenbacher and Victoria Peterson opposed piecemeal changes and urged preserving Special Use Permit public hearings. Council Members Diane Catotti, Eddie Davis, and Steve Schewel opposed short-circuiting the comprehensive JCCPC and neighborhood stakeholder process, noting the applicant could seek a Special Use Permit instead. Catotti moved the item with the stated intention of voting no, seconded by Schewel, and the amendment failed 1-6 with only Don Moffitt voting in favor.

votes.item_title: Consistency Statement for Failed Motion: Unipole Wireless Facilities (TC1400004)
votes.notes: Adopted the alternative Attachment E consistency statement reflecting denial of the text amendment.
votes.discussion_detail: After the unipole text amendment failed, City Attorney Patrick Baker and Planning Director Steve Medlin advised Council that state statute still required adoption of the appropriate consistency statement from Attachment E corresponding to denial of the ordinance. Council briefly sought clarification because it was their first time voting on a denial consistency statement. Council Member Don Moffitt moved adoption of the denial consistency statement, seconded by Council Member Steve Schewel, and it passed unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment: Erwin Terrace at LaSalle Street (A130010)
votes.notes: Changes 19.64 acres from Urban Tier to Compact Neighborhood Tier near the planned LaSalle Street light rail station.
votes.discussion_detail: Pat Young and Aaron Cain presented A130010 to reclassify 19.64 acres at Erwin Road and LaSalle Street to the Compact Neighborhood Tier near a planned light rail station, noting a 9-1 Planning Commission recommendation and ongoing SASI/affordable housing toolbox work due January 7. Applicant team members Patrick Byker, Dan Jewell, Robinson Everett Jr., and lender Keith Wells argued the density was essential for transit and job growth, explained that lenders would not finance an air-rights wrapped parking deck project with a 15% below-market set-aside, and offered $25,000 toward the city's affordable housing toolbox plus a one-year pause on redeveloping Poplar Manor. Seven speakers from Durham People's Alliance, Durham CAN, and Durham Community Land Trustees urged Council to defer approval to negotiate permanent affordable units, arguing market-rate affordability at Duke Manor was already eroding. Mayor Bell, Eugene Brown, and Cora Cole-McFadden supported approval because 79.5% of existing units within a half-mile were already affordable and state law prohibited mandatory inclusionary zoning, whereas Diane Catotti and Steve Schewel voted no to favor holistic station-area planning and stronger affordability commitments.

votes.item_title: Zoning Map Change: Erwin Terrace at LaSalle Street (Z130031)
votes.notes: Rezones 9.86 acres to MU(D) under Compact Neighborhood standards with three added committed elements.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning staff presented companion rezoning Z130031 for 9.86 acres at Erwin Road and LaSalle Street, allowing up to 322 residential units, 260,000 sq ft of office, 45,000 sq ft of civic space, and 193,000 sq ft of commercial space cumulatively. Trustee and former UNC Law Dean Judith Welch Wegner warned that delaying the project to extract non-nexus affordable housing concessions risked unconstitutional exaction and moratorium liability, while Patrick Byker proffered $25,000 within 45 days for the city's housing toolbox and extended the Poplar Manor redevelopment hold to 18 months. Housing advocates reiterated that only 11% of half-mile units were permanently subsidized, and Council Member Steve Schewel reiterated his preference for permanent preservation while weighing job and tax base benefits. After Council Member Diane Catotti asked about the 46 projected school students and Byker proffered $23,000 for Durham Public Schools, the Council unanimously approved the rezoning 7-0.

votes.item_title: Zoning Map Change: Grandin Trace (Z130035)
votes.notes: Rezones 20.05 acres between Herndon Road and Grandale Drive to RR(D) and PDR 3.322 for up to 53-54 single-family homes.
votes.discussion_detail: Pat Young presented Z130035, correcting a staff report reference to note the proffered northbound right-turn lane on Grandale Drive onto Barbee Road, and reporting a 10-0 Planning Commission recommendation. Applicants Tony Tate and Bill Ripley noted neighborhood meetings had addressed most concerns except resident George Bryan's request for a left-turn lane on Grandale Drive at Barbee Road to curb cut-through traffic on Huntsman Drive. Transportation staff Wesley Parham explained that the development did not trigger a TIA for that off-site improvement and that NCDOT required turn lanes at the site entrance instead, while Ripley noted double-frontage screening along Grandale would replace removed pines. Council Member Don Moffitt questioned why all project traffic exited onto Grandale Drive with no access to Herndon Road and cast the lone dissenting vote as the rezoning passed 6-1.

votes.item_title: Consistency Statement: Grandin Trace (Z130035)
votes.notes: Statutory consistency statement accompanying Z130035.
votes.discussion_detail: After the City Attorney reminded Council that a consistency statement vote was also required for Item 19 and Item 18, Mayor Bell entertained a motion on the consistency statement for Grandin Trace (Z130035). The motion was moved and seconded without further debate. All seven members, including Council Member Moffitt, voted in favor, passing the consistency statement 7-0.

votes.item_title: Consistency Statement: Erwin Terrace at LaSalle Street (Z130031)
votes.notes: Delayed consistency vote for Item 18 taken after Item 19 upon City Attorney reminder.
votes.discussion_detail: Prompted by the City Attorney's reminder that Council had omitted the statutory consistency statement vote after approving Item 18 (Erwin Terrace at LaSalle Street rezoning Z130031), Mayor Bell called for a motion on the Item 18 consistency statement. The motion was moved and seconded without additional discussion. Council approved the consistency statement unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Zoning Map Change: Waffle House NC 55 Highway (Z140019)
votes.notes: Rezones 1.5 acres at 4203 NC 55 Highway from OI to CN for a Waffle House restaurant.
votes.discussion_detail: Pat Young presented Z140019 to rezone 1.5 acres at 4203 NC 55 Highway from Office Institutional to Commercial Neighborhood for a Waffle House, noting consistency with the Future Land Use Map and a 10-0 Planning Commission recommendation. Resident Sharon Maddox of 5816 Henry Place testified about severe flooding in June 2013 that caused $13,000 in damage to her home and heavy rush-hour traffic on Carpenter Fletcher Road and NC 55. Staff explained the parcel was outside the floodplain and subject to strict stormwater quality and volume rules, while Council Member Don Moffitt described modern underground detention and sand-filter requirements under Jordan and Falls Lake rules. Mayor Bell stated he remained concerned about disturbing land near a flooding-prone corridor and voted no as the rezoning passed 6-1.

votes.item_title: Consistency Statement: Waffle House NC 55 Highway (Z140019)
votes.notes: Statutory consistency statement accompanying Z140019.
votes.discussion_detail: Following passage of the NC 55 Waffle House rezoning, Mayor Bell called for a motion on the statutory consistency statement. Council Member Steve Schewel moved approval, seconded by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden. Without further debate, the Council voted unanimously 7-0 to adopt the consistency statement.

votes.item_title: Approval of Landlord's Certificate for Tenant Shannon SP Associates Limited Partnership (Item 22)
votes.notes: Supplemental agenda item.
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Bell introduced supplemental Item 22, the approval of a landlord's certificate by the City of Durham for tenant Shannon SP Associates Limited Partnership. No staff presentation or public comment was requested. Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden moved approval, seconded by Council Member Steve Schewel, and the motion passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Policy on Memorials on City Property or Right-of-Way (Pulled Consent Item 7)
votes.notes: Establishes 45-day policy for spontaneous roadside/public memorials.
votes.discussion_detail: Resident Victoria Peterson pulled Consent Item 7 to question the wording 'unauthorized memorials' in the policy's purpose statement, arguing that allowing spontaneous memorials for 45 days effectively authorized them, and urged extending the time limit and encouraging contact information on memorials. Deputy City Manager Bo Ferguson explained the policy was drafted at Council's request to provide consistent treatment across city property and rights-of-way. City Attorney Patrick Baker clarified that not every placed memorial would be automatically authorized, particularly if it obstructed rights-of-way, and Mayor Bell noted the policy applied to spontaneous voluntary memorials rather than permanent monuments. Council Member Don Moffitt moved approval, seconded by Council Member Eugene Brown, and the policy passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: FY 2014 Byrne Criminal Justice Innovation Program Planning Grant Award (Pulled Consent Item 13)
votes.notes: Accepts federal planning grant utilizing UNC-Greensboro as research partner for Census Tract 10.01.
votes.discussion_detail: Victoria Peterson pulled Consent Item 13 to challenge why federal Byrne Criminal Justice grant funds were directed to UNC-Greensboro to study Census Tract 10.01 rather than to North Carolina Central University or local youth intervention and jobs programs. Ed Sarvis of the Durham Police Department explained that the U.S. Attorney's Office referred UNC-Greensboro because of its specialized research capacity, eliminating the need for an RFP. Council Member Don Moffitt confirmed with Sarvis that zero local City of Durham dollars were required for the planning grant and that participating unlocked eligibility for $1 million in federal implementation funding. Moffitt moved approval, seconded by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden, and the motion passed 7-0.

disagreements.issue: Administrative Approval of Unipole Wireless Towers Ahead of Comprehensive WCF Revisions (TC1400004)
disagreements.summary: Council voted 1-6 to reject a private text amendment allowing unipole ('slick stick') cell towers via administrative approval in non-residential districts, choosing instead to wait for the broader wireless communication facility ordinance overhaul (TC120013).
disagreements.side_a_position: Wait for comprehensive wireless ordinance revisions (TC120013) and retain Special Use Permit public hearings.
side_a_arguments: Approving a single-company text amendment would short-circuit months of stakeholder engagement by JCCPC, staff, and neighborhood groups on TC120013.
The comprehensive overhaul is expected to require larger lots and greater setbacks than the existing UDO.
The applicant already had the option to seek a Special Use Permit before the Board of Adjustment for the specific Durham Tech site.
disagreements.side_b_position: Approve administrative approval for unipoles in non-residential zones immediately.
side_b_arguments: Waiting six months for TC120013 delays improved cellular coverage and 911 access near Durham Tech.
Unipoles conceal antennas internally and are far less visually obtrusive than monopines, which are already administratively permitted.
disagreements.resolution: Failed 1-6; Council adopted the denial consistency statement 7-0.

disagreements.issue: Erwin Terrace at LaSalle Street Compact Neighborhood Tier Expansion and Transit-Area Affordable Housing (A130010)
disagreements.summary: Council split 5-2 in approving a Comprehensive Plan amendment expanding the Compact Neighborhood Tier at Erwin Road and LaSalle Street without a binding 15% affordable housing commitment in new construction.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the Compact Neighborhood Tier expansion now without delaying for the city's affordable housing toolbox.
side_a_arguments: Approximately 2,030 units (79.5%) within a half-mile of the proposed LaSalle Street station are already affordable at 60% AMI, well above Council's 15% aggregate goal.
Lenders would not finance a complex wrapped parking deck mixed-use development with mandatory 15% below-market units, and North Carolina law prohibits mandatory inclusionary zoning.

Delaying an established local developer who applied before the May 2014 resolution—and proffered $25,000 for the housing toolbox plus a Poplar Manor redevelopment pause—would jeopardize jobs, tax base, and light rail density.
disagreements.side_b_position: Defer or reject piecemeal tier expansion until holistic station-area planning and stronger long-term affordable housing commitments are in place.
side_b_arguments: Current market-rate affordability around Duke Manor and Poplar Manor is not permanently protected and rents are already rising ahead of light rail.
Expanding the Compact Neighborhood Tier parcel-by-parcel undermines the comprehensive SASI station-area planning and affordable housing toolkit process underway for January 2015.
Keeping the hearing open could allow the developer to craft a longer-term preservation commitment for Poplar Manor once the city's incentive toolbox is ready.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 5-2; Council later voted 7-0 for the companion rezoning (Z130031) after the developer extended the Poplar Manor hold to 18 months and added a $23,000 DPS contribution.

disagreements.issue: Grandin Trace Rezoning Traffic Access on Grandale Drive (Z130035)
disagreements.summary: Council voted 6-1 to approve the 54-unit Grandin Trace single-family rezoning, with Council Member Don Moffitt dissenting over all development traffic exiting onto Grandale Drive.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the rezoning with required Grandale Drive right-turn lane and double-frontage landscaping.
side_a_arguments: The proposal is consistent with the Low-Density Residential future land use map and received a 10-0 Planning Commission recommendation.
The project does not reach the trip threshold for a TIA to require an off-site left-turn lane at Grandale and Barbee Road, which is already committed by 751 South.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose approval due to lack of Herndon Road access.
side_b_arguments: Routing all new subdivision traffic onto Grandale Drive without a connection to Herndon Road places the traffic burden solely on Grandale Drive.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 6-1.

disagreements.issue: Waffle House NC 55 Rezoning and Downstream Flooding Risks (Z140019)
disagreements.summary: Council voted 6-1 to rezone 1.5 acres on NC 55 Highway for a Waffle House, with Mayor Bill Bell dissenting over downstream flooding concerns raised by a nearby homeowner.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the Commercial Neighborhood rezoning subject to modern stormwater rules.
side_a_arguments: The site is designated Commercial on the Future Land Use Map and is outside the mapped floodplain.
Current Durham stormwater and Jordan/Falls Lake rules require engineered underground retention and filtration so post-development runoff does not exceed pre-development levels.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose rezoning due to flooding risks in the adjacent corridor.
side_b_arguments: Disturbing and paving land near Meridian Parkway and Henry Place risks worsening chronic flooding experienced by nearby residents.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 6-1.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Meeting November 17, 2014
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council presented civic honors to Sister Cities international award winners, the national-champion Durham Bullseye All-Stars youth basketball team, and surviving members of the undefeated 1943 Hillside Hornets football team. Police Chief Jose Lopez delivered the 2014 third-quarter crime and community relations report, sparking Council questions about racial disparities in vehicle searches, local police recruiting, and open internal affairs cases alongside public criticism of policing practices. Council unanimously approved the remaining consent agenda, a revised UDO text amendment on utility-easement tree replacement calculations, an amended Civilian Police Review Board procedural manual, and a Durham Tech brownfields job training contract.

agenda_items.title: Sister Cities Awards, Durham Bullseye All-Stars Recognition, and 1943 Hillside Hornets Day Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell and Sister Cities Chair Brady Surles recognized Kathy Davidson, Dr. Bill Ingram, Sister Communities of San Ramon Nicaragua, and the Latino Community Credit Union for promoting international understanding. Mayor Bell also recognized the Durham Bullseye All-Stars youth basketball team for winning a national championship, proclaimed November 25, 2014 as '1943 Hornets Day in Durham' honoring the undefeated, untied, unscored-upon 1943 Hillside High School football team, and welcomed Cub Scout Pack 424.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Adoption (excluding pulled Items 3 and 8)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Don Moffitt briefly explained the consent agenda process for visiting Cub Scouts before Mayor Bell read Items 1 through 8, including minutes, a Human Relations Commission appointment, selection of Urban Design Ventures LLC for the Five-Year Consolidated Plan, an NCDOT property exchange for the Guess Road widening and Mountains-to-Sea Trail, and HUD Fair Housing Assistance. Items 3 and 8 were pulled for public comment.

agenda_items.title: Durham Police Department Third Quarterly Report on Crime and Community Relations (2014)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Police Chief Jose Lopez reported that Part I violent crime rose 19% through Q3 (driven by aggravated assaults, though Q3 aggravated assaults fell nearly 20% from Q2), homicides stood at 17 through Q3 (20 year-to-date vs. 24 in 2013), and Priority 1 calls rose 27%. Council Member Steve Schewel praised unprecedented data transparency while flagging that African American drivers were searched six times as often as white drivers and only 16 of 73 recruit applicants were from Durham; Council Members Eddie Davis and Don Moffitt probed recruiting pipelines and 25 open internal affairs cases, while speakers Chris Tiffany and Victoria Peterson criticized police conduct and youth criminalization.

agenda_items.title: UDO Text Amendment: Tree Coverage Calculations (TC120003)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a revised private text amendment by Horvath Associates modifying UDO Section 8.3 to exempt utility easements at least 50 feet wide from tree replacement calculations exclusively for single-family residential developments, excluding tree preservation, density, and impervious surface calculations. Applicant Ron Horvath noted the revisions addressed Council feedback from February and May 2014 hearings.

agenda_items.title: Amendment to Civilian Police Review Board Procedural Manual
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speakers Victoria Peterson and Chris Tiffany pulled Item 3 to raise concerns over 16- and 17-year-old arrestees being housed in the Durham County Jail rather than youth detention and to criticize the Civilian Police Review Board for restricting public comment at its forum to two minutes. Mayor Bell proposed changing wording in HRC-22 from 'City Manager and confirmed by the City Council' to 'City Manager if confirmed by the City Council' to clarify Council authority.

agenda_items.title: Environmental Workforce Development Job Training Contract with Durham Technical Community College
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson pulled Item 8 to ask whether Brownfields job training outreach reached McDougald Terrace, prioritized ex-offenders, and offered evening classes or literacy support. Workforce coordinator Allen Wimmer confirmed orientation sessions were held at McDougald Terrace, approximately 15 former offenders participated in the third cohort, and the program served adults aged 18 and older.

votes.item_title: Approval of Consent Agenda (Items 1-8, excluding Items 3 and 8)
votes.notes: Items 3 and 8 were pulled for separate discussion.
votes.discussion_detail: After Council Member Don Moffitt explained the consent agenda procedure to visiting Cub Scouts from Pack 424, Mayor Bell read Consent Agenda Items 1 through 8, including meeting minutes, a Human Relations Commission appointment, a contract with Urban Design Ventures LLC for the Five-Year Consolidated Plan and Fair Housing Analysis, an NCDOT property exchange for the Guess Road widening project and Mountains-to-Sea Trail, and the HUD Fair Housing Assistance Program. Items 3 (Civilian Police Review Board manual) and 8 (Durham Tech job training contract) were pulled for public comment. A motion to approve the remaining consent items was made and seconded, passing unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: UDO Text Amendment: Tree Coverage Calculations (TC120003)
votes.notes: Applies utility-easement exemption (>=50 ft wide) only to tree replacement calculations in single-family residential developments.
votes.discussion_detail: Michael Stock of the Planning Department presented revised UDO Text Amendment TC120003, originally heard on February 3 and May 19, 2014, by Horvath Associates to amend Section 8.3 tree protection and coverage rules. Following earlier Council comments, the applicant narrowed the proposal so that utility easements of record at least 50 feet wide are exempted only from tree replacement calculations in single-family residential developments—not tree preservation, density, or impervious surface calculations. Applicant Ron Horvath explained that wide powerline easements cannot be replanted and that the revision addressed prior equity concerns raised by Council Members Schewel and Moffitt. Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden moved approval of Attachment B, seconded by Council Member Eugene Brown, and the amendment passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Consistency Statement: Tree Coverage Calculations Text Amendment (TC120003)
votes.notes: Statutory consistency statement accompanying TC120003 (Attachment C).
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately following passage of the tree coverage text amendment, Mayor Bell entertained a motion on the corresponding statement of consistency in Attachment C. Council Member Steve Schewel moved approval, seconded by Council Member Diane Catotti. Without further discussion, the Council approved the consistency statement 7-0.

votes.item_title: Amendment to Civilian Police Review Board Procedural Manual (Pulled Consent Item 3)
votes.notes: Approved with Mayor Bell's clarifying wording change regarding Council confirmation of CPRB appointments.
votes.discussion_detail: Resident Victoria Peterson pulled Item 3 to question who authorizes sending 16- and 17-year-old arrestees to the Durham County Jail rather than a youth detention facility and raised concerns about jail education, while Chris Tiffany criticized the Civilian Police Review Board for restricting public forum speakers to two minutes and urged at least three minutes for public comment. Mayor Bell asked the City Manager to follow up in writing on juvenile detention placement decisions. Turning to the manual text on Human Relations Commission recommendation HRC-22, Mayor Bell requested changing 'City Manager and confirmed by the City Council' to 'City Manager if confirmed by the City Council' so confirmation was not implied as a foregone conclusion. A motion to approve the manual with that wording change was made, seconded, and passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Environmental Workforce Development Job Training Contract with Durham Technical Community College (Pulled Consent Item 8)
votes.notes: Brownfields environmental job training partnership with Durham Tech for adults 18 and older.
votes.discussion_detail: Victoria Peterson pulled Consent Item 8 to ask whether the Brownfields-funded environmental workforce job training program conducted outreach in public housing such as McDougald Terrace, prioritized former offenders, and provided literacy support or evening classes for young adults with criminal records. Allen Wimmer of the Office of Economic and Workforce Development responded that staff issued press releases and held orientation sessions directly at McDougald Terrace, enrolled roughly 15 self-attested former offenders in the most recent cohort without conducting disqualifying background checks, and served participants aged 18 and older. Peterson urged continued priority for ex-offenders and evening offerings. Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden moved approval of the contract with Durham Tech, seconded by Council Member Eugene Brown, and the motion passed 7-0.

meetings.title: Durham City Council November 3, 2014
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council opened with an Ebola preparedness briefing from Duke University Health System and Durham County Public Health officials following a negative rule-out evaluation of a Person County patient, and held a moment of silence honoring late former Council Member Chuck Grab for his role in financing the Durham Bulls Athletic Park. Council unanimously approved all consent and priority items as well as four public-hearing planning measures, including an industrial buffer text amendment for Wendy's, the 175-unit Barbee Road/NC 54 multi-family rezoning, and the Comprehensive Plan amendment and 122-acre rezoning for The Corners at Brier Creek. Following a pulled consent discussion on minority workforce recruitment with engineering firm CDM Smith Inc. and public demands for local Black employment, Council unanimously awarded the Durham Central Park waterline design contract.

agenda_items.title: Ebola Preparedness and Screening Briefing by Duke Health and Durham County Public Health
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Monte Brown of Duke University Health System and Durham County Public Health Director Gayle Harris briefed the Council on regional Ebola readiness after a Person County resident with travel history to Liberia and a fever was safely transported to a dedicated, isolated Duke ICU unit and tested negative. Council members thanked Duke and County Public Health for transparent communication, dedicated transport protocols, and inter-agency coordination.

agenda_items.title: Schewel Challenge Run, Tribute to Former Council Member Chuck Grab, and Election Reminder
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Steve Schewel read into the record the 36 city employees who participated in the third annual Schewel Challenge five-mile run. Council Member Eugene Brown and Mayor Bell paid tribute to late former Council Member Chuck Grab, recounting how Grab and Mayor Harry Rodenhizer used Certificates of Participation to build the Durham Bulls Athletic Park and spark American Tobacco's redevelopment, followed by a moment of silence, and Council Member Diane Catotti reminded residents to vote on November 4.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items: Deferral of Item 7 and Additional Information on Item 12 (Musco Sports Lighting)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager reported that Item 7 (neighborhood revitalization small project development guidelines) was deferred to the November 6 work session for possible rule suspension and vote, and provided supplemental information for Item 12 (Musco Sports Lighting LLC contract for Garrett Road Park tennis courts). Council approved the City Manager's priority items report 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Adoption (including Item 12; excluding deferred Item 7 and pulled Item 8)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read Consent Agenda Items 1 through 14, covering board attendance reports, Recreation and Open Space commission appointments, DCVB/TDA reappointments, street acceptances, inventory audit, Jordan Lake Partnership resolution, September bid report, Lake Michie advance land acquisition, Garrett Road Park tennis lighting (Item 12), NCDOT drainage easement dedication, and a Liberty Arts sculpture donation. Item 7 was deferred and Item 8 was pulled.

agenda_items.title: UDO Text Amendment: Industrial Light Project Boundary Buffer (TC1400002)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a private text amendment by Morningstar Law Group on behalf of Wendy's International reducing the required project boundary buffer from 100% to 40% opacity for Industrial Light parcels of four acres or less adjacent to Industrial-zoned property without a buffer, facilitating Wendy's redevelopment on Hillsborough Road. Planning Commission recommended approval 13-0.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Woodcroft / Barbee Road Residential (Z1400007)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pat Young presented a 25.35-acre rezoning at Barbee Road and NC 54 from RS-20, OI, and CN to OI(D) for up to 175 multi-family units, noting a 13-0 Planning Commission recommendation. Developer Jarod Edens noted the project reduced traffic trips compared to office uses, committed to bike lanes on Barbee Road and NC 54, and proffered $500 per projected student for Durham Public Schools prior to first site plan approval.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment: The Corners at Brier Creek (A1200008)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a 61-acre future land use amendment on US 70 near T.W. Alexander Drive consolidating commercial frontage at the intersection and shifting residential density from Low-Medium to Medium Density (6-12 units/acre). Responding to Council Member Steve Schewel's question about a Planning Commission dissent (11-2 vote), applicant attorney Patrick Byker explained the change consolidated strip commercial frontage into a nodal pattern.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: The Corners at Brier Creek (Z1200019)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pat Young presented the companion 122.2-acre rezoning at US 70 and T.W. Alexander Drive to PDR 12.0 and Commercial General for up to 603 residential units and 390,000 sq ft of non-residential space, featuring a 200-foot greenway easement and traffic mitigations. Patrick Byker highlighted reduced retail sales-tax leakage to Wake County and, at Council Member Schewel's request, proffered $10,000 ($500 per student for 20 projected students) to Durham Public Schools.

agenda_items.title: Durham Central Park Waterline Replacement Project Engineering Contract with CDM Smith Inc.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Don Moffitt and speaker Rafiq Zaidi of the FAITH coalition pulled Item 8 to scrutinize CDM Smith Inc.'s workforce diversity on the Durham Central Park waterline engineering design contract. CDM Smith Affirmative Action Manager Patrice Robbins reported Raleigh office minority representation rose from 19% to 20% (five African American staff out of 68), alongside HBCU recruitment, an NCCU hire, and MWBE subcontracts exceeding targets with CH Engineering (24%) and Roadfox (35% in construction), while Council urged CDM Smith to use City HR, Workforce Development, and YouthWorks internships.

votes.item_title: Acceptance of City Manager Priority Items (Deferral of Item 7 and Supplement for Item 12)
votes.notes: Deferred Item 7 to the November 6 work session and accepted supplemental information on Item 12 (Musco Sports Lighting LLC contract at Garrett Road Park tennis courts).
votes.discussion_detail: The City Manager presented two priority items from his October 30 memo: deferring Agenda Item 7 (guidelines for dedicated-funding small project development and neighborhood revitalization) to the November 6 work session with a request to consider suspending rules for a vote then, and providing supplemental information for Item 12, a sports lighting contract with Musco Sports Lighting LLC for Garrett Road Park tennis courts. Mayor Bell entertained a motion on the City Manager's priority items. Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden moved approval, seconded by Council Member Diane Catotti, and the motion passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: UDO Text Amendment: Industrial Light Project Boundary Buffer (TC1400002)
votes.notes: Reduces buffer opacity from 100% to 40% for IL parcels <=4 acres adjacent to Industrial-zoned parcels without a buffer.
votes.discussion_detail: Michael Stock of the Planning Department presented TC1400002, a private text amendment requested by Morningstar Law Group to reduce the required project boundary buffer from 100% to 40% opacity (with corresponding width reduction) for Industrial Light parcels of four acres or less adjacent to developed Industrial parcels lacking buffers, alongside a clarifying reorganization of UDO paragraph 9.4.3. Council Member Steve Schewel commended staff for an exceptionally clear report, and applicant attorney Patrick Byker explained the amendment would enable Wendy's to redevelop its 35-year-old Hillsborough Road restaurant rather than losing 105 feet of a 200-foot-deep lot to setbacks and an 80-foot buffer. No opponents spoke at the public hearing. Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden moved approval of Attachment B, seconded by Schewel, and the amendment passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Consistency Statement: Industrial Light Project Boundary Buffer (TC1400002)
votes.notes: Statutory consistency statement accompanying TC1400002 (Attachment C).
votes.discussion_detail: Following approval of the Industrial Light buffer text amendment, Mayor Bell called for a vote on the statutory statement of consistency found in Attachment C. Council Member Steve Schewel moved approval, seconded by Council Member Don Moffitt. Without further discussion, the Council approved the consistency statement 7-0.

votes.item_title: Zoning Map Change: Woodcroft / Barbee Road Residential (Z1400007)
votes.notes: Rezones 25.35 acres at Barbee Road and NC 54 from RS-20, OI, and CN to OI(D) for up to 175 multi-family residential units.
votes.discussion_detail: Pat Young of the Planning Department presented Z1400007, rezoning 25.35 acres at Barbee Road and NC 54 to Office Institutional with a Development Plan for up to 175 multi-family units, noting consistency with the Office future land use designation, bike-lane and right-of-way commitments, and a 13-0 Planning Commission recommendation. Applicant Jarod Edens of Edens Land Corp noted the residential plan would cut roughly 600 daily vehicle trips on NC 54 compared to commercial/office development and offered $500 per projected student for the 13 additional Durham Public Schools students. Following City Attorney clarification, Edens agreed the school contribution would be payable prior to the first site plan approval. Council Member Diane Catotti moved approval of Attachment 8, seconded by Council Member Steve Schewel, and the rezoning passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Consistency Statement: Woodcroft / Barbee Road Residential (Z1400007)
votes.notes: Statutory consistency statement accompanying Z1400007 (Attachment 9).
votes.discussion_detail: Following approval of the Barbee Road/NC 54 multi-family rezoning ordinance, Council took up the statutory statement of consistency in Attachment 9. Council Member Don Moffitt moved approval, seconded by Council Member Diane Catotti. The consistency statement passed unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment: The Corners at Brier Creek (A1200008)
votes.notes: Amends future land use map for ~61 acres at US 70 and T.W. Alexander Drive to Medium Density Residential and Commercial.
votes.discussion_detail: Pat Young presented A1200008, a Comprehensive Plan amendment for roughly 61 acres north of US 70 near T.W. Alexander Drive to intensify residential designation from 4-8 to 6-12 units per acre and reform the commercial area into a nodal pattern, reporting an 11-2 Planning Commission recommendation. Applicant attorney Patrick Byker, representing Creekwood Highway 70 Alexander LLC alongside traffic engineer Earl Lewellen, stated the amendment consolidated strip commercial frontage at the intersection and placed residential uses on environmentally sensitive terrain. Responding to Council Member Steve Schewel's inquiry about Planning Commissioner Miller's dissent, Byker argued the amendment actually reduced US 70 commercial frontage compared to current designations and fit surrounding Wake County densities. No members of the public spoke; Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden moved approval, seconded by Council Member Eugene Brown, and the motion passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Zoning Map Change: The Corners at Brier Creek (Z1200019)
votes.notes: Rezones 122.2 acres from RR to PDR 12.0 (61 acres) and CG (50.54 acres) for up to 603 residential units and 390,000 sq ft non-residential uses.
votes.discussion_detail: Pat Young presented Z1200019, the companion 122.2-acre rezoning at US 70 and T.W. Alexander Drive to PDR 12.0 and Commercial General, allowing up to 603 residential units and 390,000 sq ft of non-residential uses alongside right-of-way dedication, traffic improvements, a 200-foot greenway easement, and a 13-0 Planning Commission endorsement. Patrick Byker noted the project bridged Durham and Wake County following General Assembly boundary legislation and would capture retail sales tax leakage currently going to Raleigh's Brier Creek. At Council Member Steve Schewel's prompting, Byker committed the developer to a $10,000 Durham Public Schools contribution ($500 per projected student for 20 students) and discussed connecting greenway trails with the neighboring Del Webb Carolina Arbors community. Council Member Don Moffitt moved approval of Attachment 11 with the added proffer, seconded by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden, and the rezoning passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Consistency Statement: The Corners at Brier Creek (Z1200019)
votes.notes: Statutory consistency statement accompanying Z1200019 (Attachment 12).
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately after approving The Corners at Brier Creek rezoning, the Council voted on the required statement of consistency in Attachment 12. Council Member Don Moffitt moved approval, seconded by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden. Without further discussion, the consistency statement passed unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Durham Central Park Waterline Replacement Engineering Contract Award to CDM Smith Inc. (Pulled Consent Item 8)
votes.notes: Engineering design contract selected from 7 RFQ respondents; construction inspection amendment with Roadfox ($5,000 in design phase) to follow later.
votes.discussion_detail: Water Management Director Don Greeley introduced the engineering design contract for Durham Central Park waterline replacements, pulled by Council Member Don Moffitt and public speaker Rafiq Zaidi of the FAITH coalition, who demanded that contractors hire Black Durham residents and youth rather than excluding them. CDM Smith Affirmative Action/EEO Manager Patrice Robbins and Vice President Kevin Irby reported that Raleigh office minority staffing rose from 19% (three African Americans) to 20% (five African Americans out of 68 employees), highlighted recruitment at NC A&T, NCCU, and Southern School of Engineering, and noted MWBE participation of 24% in design (CH Engineering) and over 35% planned in construction inspection (Roadfox Construction Control Services). Council members pressed CDM Smith on Roadfox's $5,000 design-phase role versus construction-phase oversight, asked staff to track hiring for six open Raleigh positions, and urged CDM Smith to route job postings through City HR/Workforce Development and join Durham's YouthWorks internship program. Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden moved approval, seconded by Council Member Eugene Brown, and the contract passed 7-0.
